THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, FRIDAY, SEPTEMBER 25, 1936

TOKYO BANS "FORTUNE"
Prohibited Photographs Printed
in American Magazine

Tokyo, Sept. 24.
An official order here to-day
banned the September issue of the
American magazine "Fortune" from
Japan. The September issue of the
magazine was devoted almost en-
tirely to articles on Japan. A
spokesman for the government ex-
plained that the magazine had been
banned because of prohibited photo-
graphs printed in the current issue.
—United Press.

The following article is extracted from "Fortune",
an American Magazine dated February, 1935:-

THE MANCHURIAN MUDDLE

The Japanese Army experiments in state socialism.

Manchukuo's bandits, bank notes, boom.

And her two great men: Chen and Minami.

On a bitterly cold day in March, 1934, a mild,
bespectacled Chinese youth, robed in multicolored silks,
solemnly ascended a flight of steps leading to the top of
a curious terraced affair of brick and earth. The wind
whistled over the bleak Manchurian plain, a pale sun shone
wintrily in the heavens, the small group around the steps
watched silently as the young man went through the tradition-
al ceremonies that made him God's Regent on Earth. It
was a cynical little gathering - Japanese officers who had
put him there, Chinese officials who hoped to line their
pockets with new-regime gold, silk-hatted foreign correspond-
ents who made no effort to conceal their skepticism.
The ceremony over, the youth descended the steps
and entered a bulletproof American limousine. No cheering
populace greeted him. His subjects, indeed, had been
carefully kept at a distance. The car drove rapidly back
to the imperial "Palace", a soldier stiffly at attention
every few feet of the five-mile drive. The Manchurian
troops, 50,000 of them, kept an eye on such Manchurian
subjects as ventured outdoors that day, and seasoned
Japanese soldiers in a one-to-three mixture were posted to
keep an eye on the native troops. Everyone breathed easier
once the Emperor was back safe in his palace. There he
ascended a "dragon throne," like the terraced "altar of
heaven" a makeshift imitation of the real thing in Peiping.
Thus Pu Yi, twice Emperor of China, became Kang Teh (
("Tranquility Virtue"), first Emperor of Manchukuo. A
Manchu ruled once more in Manchuria, and the mighty line
of Manchu Emperors had come full circle.

（批：Reg. Please file. MS）

The land over which Emperor Kang Teh rules, with
some assistance from the Japanese, has been compared to an
autumn leaf. The stem is the Kwantung Peninsula, the
veins are the rivers and railroads that twist over the great
Manchurian plain, and the curled edges are the mountain
ranges that bound Manchuria. It is a large land, as big
as France and Germany together. Its life is organized
around its skeleton of railroads, along which the 28,000,000
Chinese farmers, who raise 60 per cent of the world's
soybeans, have settled. The backbone of the rail system
is the great T formed by the Russian-dominated Chinese
Eastern Railway, which runs west-east across the land, and
the Japanese-owned South Manchuria Railway (S.M.R.), which
strikes north from Dairen to meet it. At the juncture of
the T is Harbin, 405,000 population, focus of the Russian
influence and center of the important Sungari River traffic.
All the other big cities and all the industries center
around the S.M.R. zone: Hsinking, 167,000 population, the
raw, booming new capital; Mukden (389,000), strategic center
of Manchukuo's imports and exports pass; the Fushun coal
mines and oil-shale works, the iron mines and steel works
at Anshan, the iron and coal of Penhsihu; and finally, the
1,300 square miles of the Kwantung Leased Territory, which
Japan acquired in 1905.

满洲的乱局

日本军队在国家社会主义方面的实验。

满洲国的土匪、纸币与繁荣。

以及她的两位大人物：陈与南次。

在1934年3月一个严寒的日子里，一位温和、戴着眼镜、身着五彩丝绸长袍的中国青年，庄严地走上一段通向一座奇特的砖土阶梯状建筑顶部的台阶。寒风呼啸着掠过荒凉的满洲平原，苍白的太阳在天空中散发着冬日的寒意，台阶周围的一小群人默默注视着这位年轻人完成使他成为上帝在人间的摄政王的传统仪式。这是一个充满 cynicism（愤世嫉俗/冷嘲热讽）的小型集会——包括将他扶上宝座的日本军官、指望在新政权中捞取黄金的中国官员，以及毫不掩饰其怀疑态度的戴着丝质礼帽的外国记者。
仪式结束后，这位青年走下台阶，进入一辆防弹的美国豪华轿车。没有欢呼的民众迎接他。事实上，他的臣民被小心翼翼地保持在远处。汽车迅速驶回皇家“宫殿”，在五英里的路程中，每隔几英尺就有一名士兵僵硬地立正敬礼。五万名满洲军队监视着那天冒险外出的满洲臣民，而经验丰富的日本士兵则以一比三的比例混编其中，负责监视这些本地部队。一旦皇帝安全回到宫中，每个人都松了一口气。在那里，他登上了一座“龙椅”，就像那座阶梯状的“天坛”一样，是对北平真实天坛的临时仿制品。就这样，曾两次成为中国皇帝的溥仪，成为了康德（“安宁之德”），满洲国的第一任皇帝。满族人再次统治满洲，强大的满清皇帝世系完成了一个轮回。

（批注：登记。请归档。MS）

康德皇帝在日本人的某些协助下统治的土地，曾被比作一片秋叶。叶柄是关东半岛，叶脉是蜿蜒穿过广阔满洲平原的河流和铁路，卷曲的边缘则是环绕满洲的山脉。这是一片广袤的土地，面积相当于法国和德国之和。其生活围绕着作为骨架的铁路网组织起来，沿着铁路定居的是2800万中国农民，他们种植了世界60%的大豆。铁路系统的骨干是由俄国人控制的中东铁路（由西向东横贯该地区）与日本人所有的南满洲铁道株式会社（简称“满铁”，S.M.R.，从大连向北延伸与之交汇）构成的巨大“T”字形。在“T”字的交汇处是哈尔滨，人口40.5万，是俄国影响力的焦点，也是重要的松花江交通中心。所有其他大城市和所有工业都集中在满铁区域周围：新京，人口16.7万，这座粗糙、繁荣的新首都；奉天（38.9万），满洲国进出口的战略枢纽；抚顺的煤矿和油页岩工厂，鞍山的铁矿和钢铁厂，本溪湖的铁和煤；最后是日本于1905年获得的1300平方英里的关东租借地。

If you are looking for "local color" the cities
of Manchukuo may disappoint you. There are plenty of
tumbling down Chinese houses and gaudy, smelly Chinese
shops, but the travelers's dominant impression is how much
it all resembles Bridgeport, Connecticut. This
disillusion reaches its height in Dairen, from the
factories and oil tank farms on its outskirts to the
inevitable Yamato Hotel fronting on its inevitable circular
park in the well-swept, asphalted heart of the city.
Dairen even has its Atlantic City - the seaside summer
resort of Hoshigaura, complete with a luxurious Yamato
Hotel and a fine big golf course. In Mukden, contrast
is especially sharp between the neat, modern "New Town"
within the S.M.R. zone and the dusty, ramshackle Chinese
" Old Town" walled in by crumbling bricks. In the New
Town one is conscious of the big S.M.R. medical college,
which specializes in research into Asiatic diseases, of
the National City Bank, of broad streets and solid urban
buildings. In the Old Town one wanders through miles of
flimsy Chinese shops, for Mukden is the great shopping
center for Chinese goods. Hsinking has all the flavor
of a frontier boom town. New buildings are rising every-
where. The lobby of the Yamato Hotel is swarming with
engineers, officers, promoters. The streets are jammed
long after dark with shoppers spending money in handfuls,
There is a Neon-lit movie palace with an interpreter
standing beside the screen to explain American talkies to
the audience. There is a big modernistic geisha house,
where a live tree grows out of the floor and all the
Japanese dancing girls have colds through the long
Manchurian winters. Harbin, where Russian droshkies
share the streets with Chinese coolies, is no longer the
gayest city of Asia. But it still has its swanky Sungari
River Yacht Club, which would not be out of place on the
north shore of Long Island, its Russian night clubs,
most famed of which is the Club Fantasia, and its large
fur shops, where White Russians make a few yen out of the
Japanese passion for furs.
Outside the cities, Manchukuo has little in
common with Bridgeport, Connecticut. The former Chinese
province of Jehol is famous for its fields of white opium
poppies and its high smallpox rate. The whole northern
area, consisting of most of Heilungkiang and Kirin
provinces, is still pure frontier, a region of trackless
forests and mighty rivers. Over the grasslands of
Hsingan province roam nomadic Mongol herdsmen, living as
their ancestors did in the days of Tamerlane and Genghis
Khan. So the general picture is a core of Japanese
industrialization - the S.M.R. zone- a middle ground of
soybean fields patiently tilled by Chinese farmers, and
an outer frontier district of mountains, Mongols, bandits,
and shaggy-haired Manchurian tigers.
Up to the turn of the century the world regarded
Manchuria with perfunctory interest. The Manchu
Emperors who ruled over China from the seventeenth to the
twentieth centuries used their homeland chiefly as a
hunting preserve and a reservoir of Manchu "Bannermen"
to support the Dragon Throne. Chinese immigration was
actually forbidden during most of that period. But
toward the end of the nineteenth century Manchuria began
to come into her own. The first tides of Chinese
immigration flooded over her fertile plains, and the
Asiatic powers began to realize her economic and
strategic possibilities. Japan declared a war on China
and won it in five months - August to December, 1894.

如果你在寻找“地方色彩”，满洲国的城市可能会让你失望。那里有很多破败的中国房屋和花哨、气味难闻的中国商店，但旅行者最深刻的印象是这一切多么像康涅狄格州的布里奇波特（Bridgeport）。这种幻灭感在大连达到了顶峰，从其郊区的工厂和油罐区，到该市清扫干净、铺设沥青的中心地带那不可避免的圆形公园前那家不可避免的大和酒店。大连甚至拥有自己的大西洋城——星浦海滨避暑胜地，配有豪华的大和酒店和一个漂亮的大型高尔夫球场。在奉天，满铁区域内整洁现代的“新市”与由 crumbling bricks（残破砖块）围起来的尘土飞扬、摇摇欲坠的中国“旧市”之间，对比尤为鲜明。在新市，人们会注意到专门研究亚洲疾病的大型满铁医学院、花旗银行（National City Bank）、宽阔的街道和坚固的城市建筑。在旧市，人们漫步于绵延数英里的简陋中国商店之间，因为奉天是中国商品的大型购物中心。新京具有边疆繁荣城镇的所有韵味。新建筑随处可见。大和酒店的大堂里挤满了工程师、军官和 promoters（投机商/ promoter）。天黑很久之后，街道上仍然挤满了大把花钱的购物者。这里有一座霓虹灯闪烁的电影宫，屏幕旁站着一名解说员，向观众解释美国有声电影。这里有一座大型现代主义艺伎馆，地板中央长着一棵活树，所有的日本舞女在漫长的满洲冬季都患上了感冒。哈尔滨，那里俄国马车与中国苦力共享街道，已不再是亚洲最欢乐的城市。但它仍然拥有其时髦的松花江游艇俱乐部，即便放在长岛北岸也毫不逊色；还有其俄国夜总会，其中最著名的是幻想俱乐部（Club Fantasia）；以及大型皮草店，白俄商人利用日本人对皮草的热情赚取少许日元。
在城市之外，满洲国与康涅狄格州的布里奇波特几乎没有共同之处。前中国省份热河以其白色的鸦片罂粟田和高天花发病率而闻名。整个北部地区，包括黑龙江和吉林两省的大部分，仍然是纯粹的边疆，是一片无边无际的森林和强大河流的区域。在兴安省的草原上，游牧的蒙古牧民四处游荡，过着他们的祖先在帖木儿和成吉思汗时代的生活。因此，总体图景是：核心是日本工业化区域——满铁区；中间地带是中国农民耐心耕种的大豆田；外围边疆地区则是山脉、蒙古人、土匪和毛发蓬乱的满洲虎。
直到世纪之交，世界对满洲的兴趣还只是敷衍了事。十七至二十世纪统治中国的满清皇帝主要将他们的 homeland（故土）用作狩猎保护区和供养龙庭的满洲“八旗兵”储备库。在那段时期的大部分时间里，实际上禁止汉人移民。但在十九世纪末，满洲开始崭露头角。第一批中国移民潮涌过其肥沃的平原，亚洲列强开始意识到其经济和战略潜力。日本对华宣战，并在五个月内获胜——1894年8月至12月。

She took Formosa and would have bitten off a good chunk of
Manchuria had not Russia and the other powers intervened.
Forty years later the powers found her less tractable.
Having, for the moment, kept Japan out, Russia stepped in,
converting Manchuria into virtually a Russian province.
Then came the Russo-Japanese War, which ended in 1905 with
Japan's taking over the Kwantung Leased Territory and most
of the southern branch of the Chinese Eastern Railway
(which she remodeled into the S.M.R.). Japan has never
forgotten that the bones of 100,000 of her soldiers lay on
the plains of Manchuria after that war.
Of some slight aid to the Japanese during the war
had been a bold, bloody Manchruiian bandit named Chang Tso-
lin. After the war Chang, being at least as bloodthirsty
as and considerably smarter than his fellow bandit leaders,
waxed steadily in stature. To him the Manchus confided
the task of defending their home province against the rising
tide of revolution. This he faithfully did until he was
convinced that the republicans were going to win out,
whereupon he gracefully bowed to circumstances and delivered
Manchuria to them. With equal grace, they recognized
Chang's power as a fait accompli and made him Inspector
General of Manchuria.
By 1934 Chang had grown so great that he marched
his troops south of the Great Wall into Peiping and made
himself ruler of all northern China. The illiterate son
of a coolie, he lived in great style in Peiping, whose
streets were scattered with golden sand whenever he passed
over them. His amusements included playing mahjong for
princely stakes, keeping a harem of Chinese, Russian, and
English women, and giving state banquets at which cups of
warm tiger's blood were served and perhaps the head of a
guest or two chopped off pour encourager les autres.
A clever negotiator, Old Chang played the Japanese game,
though he was never a very trustworthy ally. Finally the
Japanese grew bored with Chang and his double-crossings.
In 1928 the armies of the Kuomintang came up from the South
and drove Chang back to Manchuria. Just outside of
Mukden his private train was dynamited, almost certainly
with Japanese connivance, and Chang met an end as violent
as any he had contrived for his dinner guests.
Chang was succeeded by his son, Chang Hsueh-liang,
a frail, undistinguished young man whose energy had been
sapped by debauchery and whose wits had been clouded by
opium and the teachings of the Y.M.C.A. Old Chang had
at least been willing to bargain with Japan, but Young
Chang, crammed with Y.M.C.A. idealism, was a rip-snorting
patriot. Besides, he was angry with Japan for killing
his father. Within six months the flag of the Chinese
Republic flew in Manchuria and Young Chang had declared
his allegiance to the Kuomintang Government of Chiang
Kai-shek (see Fortune, January, 1935) At once he began to
put pressure on Japan with a view to curbing her influence
and perhaps forcing her out of Manchuria altogether. He
harassed Japanese businessmen with passport difficulties
and illegal taxes. He nullified, in effect, the treaty
right of Japanese to lease land. He struck at the S.M.R.
with a system of Chinese railways which were designed to
drain traffic away from the S.M.R. and down to Newchwang
and the projected port of Hulutao, the Chinese answer to
Dairen.

她夺取了台湾，若非俄国和其他列强干预，本会咬下满洲的一大块领土。四十年后，列强发现她不再那么顺从。俄国暂时将日本拒之门外后，随即介入，将满洲 virtually（实际上）变成了俄国的一个省。随后爆发了日俄战争，战争于1905年结束，日本接管了关东租借地和大部分中东铁路南满支线（她将其改造为满铁）。日本从未忘记，在那场战争之后，十万名日本士兵的骸骨留在了满洲平原上。
在战争期间，对日本人略有援助的是一个名叫张作霖的胆大、血腥的满洲土匪。战后，张作霖至少与其他土匪头目一样嗜血，且 considerably（相当）更聪明，其地位稳步上升。满族人将保卫其家乡省份免受革命浪潮冲击的任务托付给他。他一直忠实地履行这一职责，直到他确信共和派将会获胜，于是他便优雅地向形势低头，将满洲交给了他们。同样优雅地，他们承认张作霖的权力为既成事实，并任命他为东三省巡阅使。
到1934年，张作霖的势力已如此壮大，以至于他率军南下越过长城进入北平，使自己成为整个中国北方的统治者。作为一个苦力的文盲儿子，他在北平过着奢华的生活，每当他经过时，街道上都会撒满金沙。他的娱乐活动包括以巨额赌注打麻将，养着由中国、俄国和英国女性组成的后宫，以及举办国宴，席间供应温热的虎血杯，或许还会砍下一两名客人的头颅以 pour encourager les autres（杀鸡儆猴/激励他人）。
作为一名精明的谈判者，老张与日本人周旋，尽管他从来不是一个非常可靠的盟友。最终，日本人对张作霖及其两面三刀的行为感到厌倦。1928年，国民党军队从南方北上，将张作霖赶回满洲。就在奉天城外，他的专列被炸毁，这几乎可以肯定是在日本的默许下进行的，张作霖迎来了与他曾为晚宴客人策划的同样暴烈的结局。
张作霖由其子张学良继任，这是一位体弱、不起眼的年轻人，其精力已被放荡生活耗尽，智慧也被鸦片和基督教青年会（Y.M.C.A.）的教义所蒙蔽。老张至少愿意与日本讨价还价，但小张充满了基督教青年会的理想主义，是一位狂热的爱国者。此外，他对日本杀害其父感到愤怒。六个月内，中华民国的旗帜在满洲飘扬，小张宣布效忠蒋介石的国民政府（参见《财富》杂志，1935年1月刊）。他立即开始向日本施压，旨在遏制其影响力，并可能迫使日本完全撤出满洲。他以护照困难和非法税收骚扰日本商人。他实际上废除了日本人租赁土地的权利。他通过建立一套中国铁路系统来打击满铁，该系统旨在将交通从满铁引流至营口和计划中的葫芦岛港，这是中国对大连的回应。

In such an atmosphere "incidents" multiply. By
the summer of 1931 the Japanese had collected 300 grievances
against Young Chang. Then came the killing of one
Captain Nakamura, of the Japanese Army, by some Chinese
soldiers. By the fall of 1931 the tension was unbearable.
Young Chang had frightened the capitalists and the government
of Japan, who had invested $300,000,000 in the S.M.R. and
another $200,000,000 elsewhere in Manchuria. And, what
was more dangerous, he annoyed the Japanese Army. Soon
after the killing of Captain Nakamura, the Army was
perfecting a "concrete plan for a measure to be taken
against China". And then came.....

The "incident" that never happened

THIRTY-ONE inches of rail that probably never
were blown up at all cost China Manchuria. The night of
September 18, 1931, was dark in Mukden, capital and key
city of Manchuria. Just outside the city a certain
Lieutenant Kawamoto of the Imperial Japanese Army was
practicing maneuvers with six privates along the tracks of
the Japanese-owned South Manchuria Railway. At 10:00 a.m.
they heard a loud explosion. Running to the place they
found a section of one rail blown away. They were fired
on; they returned the fire. By morning the city of Mukden
with its enormous $100,000,000 arsenal was occupied by
Japanese troops, Six months later the Japanese Army was
at the Great Wall, the native section of Shanghai had been
captured by Japanese troops, and "Manchukuo" had been
declared independent of China. A year later the Japs
had defeated General Ma, the only Chinese general to offer
effective resistance, and extended their control over
northern and western Manchuria. Early in 1933, after
a remarkable nine-day march in arctic weather, the Japanese
pushed the Chinese out of Jehol and added that Inner
Mongolian province to their new state. China had lost
Manchuria, and all for the want of thirty-one inches of
hundred-pound rail.

Why?

There is a good deal of doubt whether the
Chinese ever blew up those thirty-one inches of rail.
There is no doubt, however, that the perhaps fabulous
explosion has been costly to Japan as well as to China.
The Manchurian adventure has cost the people of Japan
$210,000,000 in direct "emergency" expenses, 10,000 killed
and wounded, and enormous indirect expenses in the way
of unprecedented increases in military expenditures.
Recently the Cabinet was bullied into voting $297,000,000
for next year's Army and Navy expenses. This was almost
half the total budget and the biggest military appropriation
in the history of the empire. Manchukuo has also cost
Japan the goodwill of almost the entire civilized world and
her seat in the League of Nations. It has cost her
merchants some 50 per cent of their trade with their second
biggest customer, China. Why has Japan poured out so
much blood and treasure? Her fears for her Manchurian
investment were a potent immediate cause, but we must dig
much deeper than that.

Not to colonize

The pat answer is that Japan wants Manchuria
for colonization. As everyone knows, the Japanese are
crowded in their four tiny islands, 450 human beings to

在这种氛围下，“事件”层出不穷。到1931年夏，日本人对张学良（Young Chang）已积累了300项不满。随后发生了一些中国士兵杀害日本陆军中尉中村（Nakamura）的事件。到了1931年秋，紧张局势已令人无法忍受。张学良吓坏了在日本南满铁路（S.M.R.）投资了3亿美元、在满洲其他地区另投资2亿美元的日本资本家和日本政府。而且，更危险的是，他惹恼了日本军队。在中村中尉被杀后不久，日军正在完善一项“针对中国采取行动的具体计划”。接着便是____

从未发生的“事件”

三十一英寸的铁轨，可能根本未曾被炸毁，却使中国失去了满洲。1931年9月18日的夜晚，满洲的首都和关键城市沈阳（Mukden）漆黑一片。就在城外，日本帝国陆军的一名河本（Kawamoto）中尉正率领六名士兵沿日本所有的南满铁路轨道进行演习。上午10:00，他们听到一声巨响。跑到现场后，发现一段铁轨被炸飞。他们遭到射击；随即还击。到天亮时，拥有价值1亿美元巨大军火库的沈阳城已被日军占领。六个月后，日军兵临长城，上海华界被日军攻占，“满洲国”宣布脱离中国独立。一年后，日本人击败了马将军——唯一提供有效抵抗的中国将领——并将其控制范围扩展至满洲北部和西部。1933年初，经过在极寒天气中非凡的九天行军，日本人将中国人赶出了热河（Jehol），并将这个内蒙古省份并入其新建立的国家。中国失去了满洲，而这一切仅仅是因为缺少了三十一英寸重的百磅钢轨。

为什么？

中国人是否真的炸毁了那三十一英寸铁轨，存在很大疑问。然而，毫无疑问的是，这场或许纯属虚构的爆炸对日本和中国都代价高昂。满洲冒险行动使日本人民直接支出了2.1亿美元的“紧急”费用，伤亡人数达1万人，并因军费空前增加而产生了巨大的间接费用。最近，内阁被迫投票批准明年陆海军经费2.97亿美元。这几乎占总预算的一半，也是帝国历史上最大的一笔军事拨款。满洲国还使日本失去了几乎整个文明世界的好感及其在国际联盟中的席位。它使其商人失去了与其第二大客户中国之间约50%的贸易额。日本为何要付出如此多的鲜血和财富？其对满洲投资的担忧是一个有力的直接原因，但我们需要挖掘得更深。

并非为了殖民

通常的回答是日本想要满洲用于殖民。众所周知，日本人在其四个小岛上拥挤不堪，每平方英里居住着450人。

the square mile. Industrialization has staved off the
famine point so far, but the land is over-burdened.
Manchuria offers vast stretches of virgin soil, fertile and
well-watered. On paper it looks like a deal.
But, unhappily, the Japanese are not a colonizing
people. One of the most potent words in Japanese is
"tamashii", the feeling for home as the place where,
culturally and racially and in a family sense, one belongs.
This mystical concept prevents the Japanese from feeling
really settled anywhere outside the fatherland. Practical
considerations also play a part in Manchukuo. The climate
in Manchukuo is much colder than in Japan - the intense
cold bothered the Japanese Army in its Manchurian campaign
much more than did any Chinese opposition. And the
Chinese standard of living is so low as to make it difficult
for even the frugal Japanese to compete. Rice is "bread"
to the Japanese, but to the Manchukuoan Chinese it is
"cake", to be eaten only on state occasions. Their "bread"
is a pancake made of kaoliang. The Koreans underlive
both Chinese and Japanese.
Let Californians and Mr. Hearst scare themselves
with visions of a Japanized Pacific Coast, the fact is the
total of Japanese living outside Japan is less than 800,000.
After twenty years of colonizing efforts in Korea, only
2 per cent of the inhabitants are Japanese. (The problem,
indeed, has been how to keep the Koreans from overrunning
Japan) Since 1931 the Japanese in Manchuria have indeed
increased from 225,000 to 315,000 - but the new settlers,
like the old ones, are almost all of them officials and
businessmen. There are practically no Japanese farmers
in Manchukuo even today. The S.M.R. spent some $1,400,000
subsidizing groups of armed colonists, but results were so
poor that it has abandoned the project. Colonization
therefore can hardly be Japan's motive.

Not to exploit

MANCHURIA has been described by writers who should
know better as a treasure chest of nature bursting with
coal, iron, wheat, gold, and all things nice. Japan
sorely needs raw materials. She imports both in quantities
so huge that only her enormous exports of manufactures
enable her to keep going. If Manchuria were as rich as
she has been painted it would be obvious why Japan lusted
after her. But she isn't. Japan needs coking coal, iron,
oil, cotton, wool, fertilizers, timber. To what extent
can Manchuria supply her needs?
Coal. The Fushun mines, owned by S.M.R., center
around the biggest open-cut coal mine in the world. They
produce 6,600,000 tons of the total 9,500,00 Manchurian
annual production. Their coal is mined cheaply enough
to undersell Japanese coal in Japan, but it is of poor
coking quality and hence of little use in smelting iron.
And coking coal is what Japan needs. She has enough
ordinary coal - the 6 per cent she gets from Manchuria is
imported solely because of its low price. Manchuria has
large coal reserves, but what little is known about their
quality is discouraging.
This is also a good place to note that in coal,
as in other commodities, Japan was getting all she wanted
from Manchuria before 1931. Setting up a puppet state
makes Manchurian oil and iron no cheaper to Japan, nor
does it affect the price of soybeans.
Oil. This is probably Japan's most pressing need,
especially from the standpoint of national defense. She
imports 90 per cent of her oil, a state of affairs all the

工业化迄今避免了饥荒临界点，但土地负担过重。满洲提供了大片肥沃且水源充足的处女地。从纸面上看，这似乎是一笔划算的交易。
但不幸的是，日本人并不是一个善于殖民的民族。日语中最有力的词汇之一是“魂”（tamashii），即把家视为在文化、种族和家庭意义上归属的地方。这种神秘的概念阻止了日本人在祖国以外的任何地方真正安顿下来。实际考虑也在满洲国问题上起作用。满洲国的气候比日本冷得多——严寒给日军在满洲战役中带来的困扰远甚于任何中国人的抵抗。而且，中国人的生活水平如此之低，以至于即使节俭的日本人也难以与之竞争。米饭对日本人来说是“面包”，但对满洲国的中国人来说却是“蛋糕”，仅在重大场合食用。他们的“面包”是一种用高粱制成的饼。朝鲜人的生活水平低于中国人和日本人。
让加利福尼亚人和赫斯特先生（Mr. Hearst）去为日本化的太平洋海岸景象感到恐慌吧，事实是居住在日本境外的日本人总数不到80万。在经过二十年的朝鲜殖民努力后，居民中只有2%是日本人。（事实上，问题一直是如何防止朝鲜人涌入日本）自1931年以来，满洲的日本人确实从22.5万增加到了31.5万——但新移民像旧移民一样，几乎全是官员和商人。即使在今天，满洲国也几乎没有日本农民。南满铁路花费了约140万美元资助武装殖民团体，但由于结果太差，已放弃了该项目。因此，殖民很难说是日本的动机。

并非为了剥削

一些本应更知情的作家将满洲描述为一个充满煤炭、铁、小麦、黄金和所有美好事物的自然宝库。日本急需原材料。她进口的数量如此巨大，只有依靠庞大的制成品出口才能维持运转。如果满洲真如描绘的那样富饶，日本对其垂涎欲滴的原因就显而易见了。但事实并非如此。日本需要炼焦煤、铁、石油、棉花、羊毛、肥料、木材。满洲能在多大程度上满足她的需求？
煤炭。由南满铁路所有的抚顺煤矿，围绕著世界上最大的露天煤矿展开。其产量为660万吨，占满洲年总产量950万吨的大部分。其煤炭开采成本足够低，能在日本以低于日本煤的价格销售，但其炼焦质量较差，因此在炼铁方面用途不大。而日本需要的正是炼焦煤。她有足够的普通煤——从满洲获得的6%进口 solely 是因为其价格低廉。满洲拥有丰富的煤炭储量，但对其质量的少量了解令人沮丧。
这也是一个指出以下事实的好地方：在煤炭以及其他商品方面，日本在1931年之前就从满洲获得了她想要的一切。建立一个傀儡国家并没有使满洲的石油和铁对日本来说更便宜，也没有影响大豆的价格。
石油。这可能是日本最迫切的需求，特别是从国防角度来看。她进口90%的石油，这种情况更加可怕，因为她的军事力量消耗了其总消费量的三分之一以上。

more appalling because her military forces use a good
third of her total consumption. No oil wells have yet
been found in Manchuria but the Fushun coal is overlaid
by oil-bearing shale, and in 1929 a big oil-extraction
plant was erected there. It is, however, an enormously
expensive process and the plant has never been a commercial
success. Operated at capacity, it would supply less than
10 per cent of Japan's annual consumption. The S.M.R.,
on the other hand, estimates that its Fushun shale reserves
are enough to supply all Japan's needs for a century - if the
government could feet the bill that long. At present
the Fushun deposits are worked for strategic rather than
commercial reasons: the Japanese Navy obligingly takes
the entire output of Fushun oil at cost.
Iron. Equally essential to Japan's peacetime economy
and her preparations for war is iron, and here too she
faces a serious shortage at home. Over 90 per cent of
the iron she uses is imported. The big Manchurian iron
mines are at Anshan, with Penhsihu a very poor second,
but both produce ore of such low quality - 30 to 40 per
cent iron content - that Western countries would not bother
to mine it. The silicon content is high, a drawback in
using it for steel. Like the oil-recovery plant, the
Anshan works run at a loss which is borne in the end by
the Japanese Government. Again, as with oil, Manchukuo's
iron reserves are enough to supply Japan for centuries -
but the cost would be staggering. Military necessity,
however, laughs at economics, and by the end of 1934 the
S.M.R. expected to have in operation at Anshan the Showa
Steel Works, which will be the second largest steel plant
in the Far East.
Agriculture. Ironically enough, it is as a source
of food supply that Manchuria seems to promise most to
Japan, and it is precisely here that she is least needed.
Although Japan has a big trade deficit in foodstuffs, the
problem at present is not acute. Rice is her main need,
and she gets almost 90 per cent of her import requirements
from her colonies, Korea and Formosa. She might import
Manchurian wheat if she could induce the Manchurian
farmers to raise it. But wheat is fairly hard to raise
and the Manchurian peasant can't afford a gamble. For
his own food he raises kaoliang, whose scarlet plumed
stalks tower eight feet in the air. For his cash crop
he sticks to that amazing vegetable product, the protein
soybean (Fortune, June, 1930). Manchukuo produces 60
per cent of the world's soybean crop. The soybean is
eaten as vegetable, cheese, pickle, flour, butter, and
salad oil. It also plays industrial roles in soapmaking,
dyestuffs, plastics, etc. Its main uses, however, are
as cattle feed and as fertilizer, and the soybean is
Manchukuo's only important agricultural export to Japan.
It is mostly used as fertilizer for the little fields that
must support so great a population burden. Even this use,
however, is threatened by the development of a native
sulphate of ammonia industry - per unit of nitrogen, sulphate
of ammonia is considerably cheaper as a fertilizer than the
soybean. Almost anything can be raised on Manchukuo's
fertile, well-watered soil, and the time may come when
Manchukuo will supply more than soybeans to Japan. But
for the present only a little more than one-fifth of the
total raw foodstuffs imported into Japan comes from
Manchukuo.

满洲尚未发现油井，但抚顺煤层上覆盖着含油页岩，1929年在那里建立了一座大型提油厂。然而，这是一个极其昂贵的过程，该工厂从未在商业上取得成功。即使满负荷运转，其供应量也不足日本年消费量的10%。另一方面，南满铁路估计其抚顺页岩储量足以供应日本一个世纪的需求——如果政府能长期支付这笔费用的话。目前，开采抚顺矿床是出于战略而非商业原因：日本海军乐意按成本价收购抚顺石油的全部产量。
铁。铁对日本的和平经济及其战争准备同样至关重要，而她在国内也面临严重短缺。她使用的铁超过90%依赖进口。满洲的大型铁矿位于鞍山，本溪湖（Penhsihu）居次且状况较差，但两者生产的矿石品位极低——含铁量仅为30%至40%——西方国家甚至不屑于开采。硅含量高，这是将其用于炼钢的一个缺点。与提油厂一样，鞍山工厂也在亏损运营，最终由日本政府承担。同样，就像石油一样，满洲国的铁储量足以供应日本数个世纪——但成本将高得惊人。然而，军事必要性无视经济学，到1934年底，南满铁路预计将在鞍山运营昭和制钢所，这将成为远东第二大钢铁厂。
农业。具有讽刺意味的是，满洲作为粮食供应来源似乎对日本最有希望，而这恰恰是她最不需要的领域。虽然日本在食品贸易方面存在巨大逆差，但目前问题并不紧迫。大米是其主要需求，她近90%的进口需求来自其殖民地朝鲜和台湾。如果能说服满洲农民种植小麦，她可能会进口满洲小麦。但小麦相当难种，满洲农民负担不起这种赌博风险。为了自己的食物，他种植高粱，其鲜红的穗状茎秆高达八英尺。为了现金作物，他坚持种植那种神奇的植物产品——蛋白质大豆（《财富》杂志，1930年6月）。满洲国生产世界60%的大豆作物。大豆可作为蔬菜、奶酪、泡菜、面粉、黄油和沙拉油食用。它在肥皂制造、染料、塑料等工业中也发挥作用。然而，其主要用途是作为牲畜饲料和肥料，大豆是满洲国对日本唯一重要的农产品出口。它主要用作必须支撑如此巨大人口负担的小块田地的肥料。然而，即使是这种用途也受到本土硫酸铵工业发展的威胁——按单位氮计算，硫酸铵作为肥料比大豆便宜得多。满洲国肥沃、水源充足的土壤几乎可以种植任何东西，也许有一天满洲国会向日本提供除大豆以外的更多产品。但目前，日本进口的全部原生食品中，只有略多于五分之一来自满洲国。

Et. cetera. Japan needs cotton, not obly for her textile
mills but also to make munitions. Chaffing at the
tremendous quantities she must annually import, she hopes
to develop cotton areas in Manchukuo, plans five agricultural
experimental stations. But foreign experts are skeptical
about the chances of growing cotton so far north ....
There is one thing that Manchuria can supply to Japan and
that is timber. So far she hasn't - only some 1 per cent
of Japan's big timber imports come from Manchuria - but
her forest reserves are enormous. Once the bandits have
been suppressed, Japan should be able to get most of her
timber from Manchuria.... By encouraging the wandering
Mongol tribes in their stock raising, Japan hopes to
increase Manchuria's wood output, throw off her dependence
on Australian imports... The streams of the North yield
a little placer gold - some $2,000,000 a year. The
S.M.R. has been sending out armed groups of prospectors
but so far without making any sensational discoveries...
Magnesite fanciers will be thrilled to learn that Manchukuo's
magnesite deposits are "the best in the world" and that
reserves are calculated at 20,000,000,000 tons.

But To fight

There are those who think that the next great
war will be fought on the plains of Manchuria and Mongolia.
(See map on page 82) For Manchuria is the military key
to the Far East, a buffer state wedged between the three
major Asiatic powers: Japan, Russia, China. Whichever
of the three controls Manchuria has a first line of defense,
or offense, against the other two. To Japan especially,
with only Korea as a foothold on the continent, Manchuria
has become her "life line". If she let go, the surf of
war might sweep her off the mainland. For strategic
reasons at least Japan felt it necessary to take Manchuria
unto herself. Even the gray web of Manchurian economics
is shot through with the scarlet thread of war. Manchurian
oil and iron, as we have seen, are too expensive to interest
anyone but the soldier, who never counts the cost. The
new railroads Manchukuo is pushing over her plains, at the
rate of five miles a day, are at least as important
strategically as commercially. This, then, is one sound
explanation of Japan's interest in Manchukuo - as a theatre
of war. Already the stage is being set. Russia is
said to have from 100,000 to 200,000 troops along her
side of the border. Japan has 80,000 of her own troops
in Manchukuo today, to say nothing of 100,000 Manchukuo
troops - of whom the less said the better.

An to fulfill

But the deepest motivation of Japan's Manchurian
adventure is neither colonial nor economic nor even strategic
All this reasonable arguing about it and about is beside
the point. The Japanese Army marched through arctic
weather into every corner of Manchuria primarily because
it was driven by an urge for conquest as strong and as
irrational as any sexual libido. Freud would have
understood. The glorious, golden vision of empire was
before its eyes. The Japanese nation feels that it is
divinely ordained to rule over Asia. When America felt
that way she talked of "manifest destiny".. England
referred to "the white man's burden". Germany spoke of
"Kultur" and demanded "a place in the sun." Japan's

有一样东西是满洲能够供应给日本的，那就是木材。迄今为止她尚未做到——日本大量的木材进口中只有约 1% 来自满洲——但她的森林储量巨大。一旦土匪被镇压，日本应该能够从满洲获得其大部分木材 ____ 通过鼓励游牧的蒙古部落从事畜牧业，日本希望增加满洲的木材产量，摆脱对澳大利亚进口的依赖……北方的河流出产少量砂金——每年约值 2,000,000 美元。南满铁路公司（S.M.R.）一直派出武装探矿队，但至今未取得任何轰动性的发现……菱镁矿爱好者将会兴奋地得知，满洲国的菱镁矿矿藏是“世界上最好的”，储量估计为 20,000,000,000 吨。

但是为了战争

有些人认为，下一次大战将在满洲和蒙古的平原上打响。（见第 82 页地图）因为满洲是远东的军事关键，是一个夹在日本、俄罗斯、中国这三个亚洲主要强国之间的缓冲国。这三国中无论哪一国控制满洲，就拥有针对其他两国的第一道防线或进攻线。特别是对日本而言，在大陆上仅以朝鲜为立足点，满洲已成为她的“生命线”。如果她放手，战争的浪潮可能会将她从大陆冲走。至少出于战略原因，日本觉得有必要将满洲据为己有。即使是满洲错综复杂的经济网络，也交织着战争的猩红丝线。如我们所见，满洲的石油和铁太过昂贵，除了从不计较成本的军人外，引不起任何人的兴趣。满洲国正以每天五英里的速度在其平原上推进的新铁路，至少在战略上与商业上同样重要。那么，这就是解释日本对满洲国兴趣的一个有力理由——将其作为战场。舞台已经在搭建。据说俄罗斯在其边境一侧部署了 100,000 至 200,000 名军队。日本今天在满洲国有 80,000 名自己的军队，更不用说 100,000 名满洲国军队——对此最好少说为妙。

以及为了实现

但是，日本满洲冒险的最深层动机既非殖民性质，也非经济性质，甚至非战略性质。所有关于此的合理争论都不得要领。日本军队之所以冒着极寒天气进军满洲的每一个角落，主要是因为它被一种征服欲所驱使，这种欲望如同任何性本能一样强烈且非理性。弗洛伊德会理解这一点。辉煌的金色帝国愿景就在眼前。日本民族感到自己受命于天，要统治亚洲。当美国有这种感觉时，她谈论的是“天命昭彰”……英国指的是“白人的负担”。德国谈论的是“文化”并要求“阳光下的地盘”。日本的

page_data.en:
- 8 -

less imaginative catchwords are "Asia for the Asiatics,"
"Japanism". When men lust after women or nations after
empires, they don't act or talk rationally. For five
hours the eminent but drearily reasonable gentlemen of the
Lytton Commission once sat and listened to the voluble
explanation of one of Japan's leading statesmen. They
were embarrassed to find that they just couldn't make
sense out of the harangue. For the deepest roots of Japan's
Manchurian policy lie far beneath the surface of conscious
expression. They draw strength from a supra-rational,
almost mystical Nietzschean will to power.
Our thread of reasoning has led us to the very
heart of the Manchurian labyrinth, where dwells a fearsome
Minotaur indeed: the Imperial Japanese Army. The two
strongest motives for taking over Manchuria, military
strategy and sheer lust for empire, are precisely those
that act the most powerfully on the Army. And the Army
happens to be the most potent force in contemporary Japan.

The Army is boss

In the summer of 1931 a tense little group of
young Army officers waited on Premier Wakatsuki. Earnestly
they presented him with the "300 incidents", a list of
Manchurian insults to Japan that they had drawn up, and
earnestly they begged for war. Their request was refused.
When Captain Nakamura was killed by Manchurian soldiers
some weeks later, the Japanese Army began negotiations
with China independently of the Japanese Government.
When the Army's demands were not satisfied it proceeded to
put into execution a carefully prepared plan of attack.
It was so exclusively an Army show that in the early stages
Japanese Consuls in Manchuria were as much in the dark as
everyone else. For the next few months the world witnessed
the incredible spectacle of a pacifistic government
trying vainly to restrain its own armies.
The Wakatsuki Cabinet, like all succeeding
Cabinets, had neither the legal nor the moral power to curb
the Army. The Army occupies a unique place in Japan.
It takes its order neither from the Cabinet nor from the
Parliament but direct from the Emperor. The military
heads, like the Premier, are responsible only to the Emperor,
which, with all respect to their veneration for the Son of
Heaven, means they are responsible only to themselves.
The Ministers of War and Navy, furthermore, (1) must be
a general and an admiral respectively, (2) do not have to
resign when a Cabinet falls, and (3) have the right to appeal
direct to the Emperor. Thus the military, controlled
only by an unambitious Son of Heaven, can, and do, act
pretty much as they please.
But the power of the Army goes far beyond legal
forms. The Japanese people have had very little experience
of either capitalism or democracy, and what little they
have had has been disillusioning. The Japanese version
of capitalism has brought wealth to a few Mitsuis and Mit-
subishis but it has long meant grinding poverty for the
Japanese masses. The people speedily found it was useless
to turn to the politicians, who were bought up by the
capitalists almost in open market. That left only the
Emperor - and the Army. The Emperor became a fetish,
loyalty to him a mystic experience. And the Army, whose
loyalty to the Emperor is as fanatical as its hatred of
the capitalists and politicians, became the articulate
voice of the people. The nationalistic, anti-Western,

- 8 -

缺乏想象力的口号是“亚洲人的亚洲”、“日本主义”。当男人渴望女人或国家渴望帝国时，他们的言行并不理性。李顿调查团那些杰出但枯燥乏味的绅士们曾坐了五个小时，聆听日本一位主要政治家滔滔不绝的解释。他们尴尬地发现，他们根本无法从这篇长篇大论中理出头绪。因为日本满洲政策的最深层根源远在意识表达的表面之下。它们从一种超理性的、近乎神秘的尼采式权力意志中汲取力量。
我们的推理线索将我们引向了满洲迷宫的核心，那里确实居住着一个可怕的米诺陶洛斯：大日本帝国陆军。接管满洲的两个最强有力的动机——军事战略和对帝国的纯粹渴望——恰恰是对军队作用最大的因素。而军队恰好是当代日本最强大的力量。

军队是老板

1931 年夏，一群神情紧张的年轻陆军军官拜谒了若槻首相。他们郑重地向他提交了他们编制的“三百事件”，即一份满洲侮辱日本的清单，并恳求开战。他们的请求被拒绝。当中村大尉几周后被满洲士兵杀害时，日本军队开始独立于日本政府与中国进行谈判。当军队的要求未得到满足时，它便开始执行一项精心准备的攻击计划。这完全是一场军队的独角戏，在初期阶段，日本驻满洲领事与其他所有人一样被蒙在鼓里。在接下来的几个月里，世界目睹了令人难以置信的景象：一个和平主义政府徒劳地试图约束自己的军队。
若槻内阁，如同所有继任的内阁一样，既没有法律权力也没有道德权力来遏制军队。军队在日本占据着独特的地位。它不接受内阁或议会的命令，而是直接听命于天皇。军事首领与首相同样，只向天皇负责，这意味着，尽管我们要尊重他们对天子的崇敬，但实际上他们只对自己负责。此外，陆军大臣和海军大臣：(1) 必须分别由将军和海军上将担任，(2) 内阁倒台时无需辞职，以及 (3) 有权直接向天皇上诉。因此，仅受一位无意扩张的天子控制的军方，可以并且确实几乎随心所欲地行动。
但是，军队的权力远不止于法律形式。日本人民几乎没有资本主义或民主的经验，而仅有的一点经验也令人幻灭。日本版的资本主义为少数三井和三菱带来了财富，但对日本大众来说，长期意味着赤贫。人们很快发现，求助于政客是无用的，因为这些政客几乎在公开市场上被资本家收买。这就只剩下天皇和军队。天皇成为一种崇拜对象，对他的忠诚成为一种神秘体验。而军队，其对天皇的忠诚与其对资本家和政客的仇恨一样狂热，成为了人民的代言人。军队的民族主义、反西方、

page_data.en:
- 9 -

back-to-the-old-ways campaign of the Army stirred the
popular imagination. Western nations, disillusioned with
capitalism, might dabble in Socialism and Fascism. But
Japan, practically a medieval nation when Commodore
Perry's black ships cast anchor in the Bay of Yedo in
1853, has gone straight back to feudalism. The old ways
couldn't be any worse than the new ways that were forcing
farmers to eat rotten fish and sell their daughters into
Yoshiwara houses. And so when the Army decided to take
over Manchuria, the people backed it up. The new land
might offer a way out of their misery. That experts think
it won't is beside the point.
The solid backing of public opinion smoothes the
way for the Army juggernaut, but the motive power comes
from within. At the core of the Army is an ultranation-
alistic, politico-religious secret society of younger
officers, fanatics all of them, who live and die for two
potent words: Hodo, "the Way of the Perfect Emperor",
and Bushido, "the Way of the Warrior". The leader of
this sect, fiery Sadao Araki, former Minister of War,
epitomized the new feeling when he pronounced: "The spirit
of the Japanese nation is, by its nature, a thing that
must be propagated over the seven seas and extended over
the five continents. Anything that may hinder it must be
abolished.

The Puppet show

Once the Army had conquered Manchuria the question
was how to hold it. It is no news that the Army's answer
was to import from Tientsin the studious heir of the Manchus,
Pu Yi. The career of this smooth-faced, retiring youth,
who is happiest playing tennis or riding his bicycle, is
a tale straight out of E.Phillips, Oppenheim. How
he was picked out as a babe by the grim old Dowager Empress
to succeed herself, how a year after the 1911 revolution
the six-year-old boy Emperor abdicated, how he grew up in
the Forbidden City in Peiping, stripped of power but still
allowed his elaborate court, how he was married to two
ladies at the age of sixteen, how in 1935 he fled to the
Japanese Concession in Tientsin for protection, how he was
plucked thence to become chief executive of Manchukuo in
1932 and two years later to be crowned Emperor Kang Teh -
all this is a story that can only be suggested here.
The government Pu Yi now heads is, to Occidental
ways of thinking, a "puppet state". It is not even a
very magnificent puppet show. The imperial palace of
Emperor Kang Teh is a ratty, square building surrounded
by low outbuildings full of soldiers. An audience with
the last of the Manchu Emperor is not an impressive function.
From the reception room, ornamented with spittoons and
shabby leather armchairs, one passes through a cramped
corridor and up a creaky staircase to the small, low-
ceilinged audience room. A red throne stands on a dingy
red carpet and Emperor Kang Teh, looking somewhat uncomfort-
able in a military uniform, stands by the throne. He
wanted to have his capital in Mukden, traditional seat
of the Manchu Empire, but the Japs wanted a Japanese-built
capital. They decided on Changchun, whose name they
changed to Hsinking ("New Capital"). There is slight
pretense made as to who is boss in Manchukuo.

回归旧道的运动激发了大众的想象力。对资本主义感到幻灭的西方国家可能会涉足社会主义和法西斯主义。但日本，在 1853 年佩里准将的黑船在江户湾抛锚时实际上还是一个中世纪国家，已经直接回到了封建主义。旧制度不可能比迫使农民吃烂鱼并将女儿卖到吉原妓院的新制度更糟糕。因此，当军队决定接管满洲时，人民支持它。这片新土地可能为他们提供摆脱苦难的途径。专家认为这行不通，但这无关紧要。
舆论的坚实支持为军队这台压路机铺平了道路，但动力来自内部。军队的核心是一个由年轻军官组成的超民族主义、政治宗教秘密社团，他们都是狂热分子，为两个强有力的词语而生而死：王道，“完美皇帝之道”，和武士道，“武士之道”。该派系的领袖、前陆军大臣荒木贞夫，在宣称“日本民族的精神，按其本性，是一种必须传播到七大洋并扩展到五大洲的事物。任何可能阻碍它的事物都必须废除”时，体现了这种新情绪。

傀儡戏

一旦军队征服了满洲，问题就是如何守住它。众所周知，军队的答案是从天津引进那位好学的满洲继承人溥仪。这位面色光滑、性格内向的青年，最快乐的时候是打网球或骑自行车，他的职业生涯简直就像 E. 菲利普斯·奥本海姆小说中的故事。他是如何被严厉的老慈禧太后在婴儿时期选中作为继承人的，如何在 1911 年革命一年后这位六岁的男孩皇帝退位，他如何在北京紫禁城中长大，虽被剥夺权力但仍保留其繁复的宫廷，他如何在十六岁时娶了两位夫人，他如何在 1935 年为寻求保护逃往天津日租界，他如何于 1932 年被从中拉出成为满洲国执政，两年后又加冕为康德皇帝——所有这些在这里只能略作提及。
溥仪现在领导的政府，按照西方的思维方式，是一个“傀儡政权”。这甚至不是一个非常宏大的傀儡戏。康德皇帝的皇宫是一座破旧的四方形建筑，周围环绕着住满士兵的低矮附属建筑。觐见最后一位满洲皇帝并非令人印象深刻的仪式。从装饰着痰盂和破旧皮革扶手椅的接待室，穿过狭窄的走廊，走上嘎吱作响的楼梯，到达低矮天花板的小觐见室。红色的宝座立在肮脏的红地毯上，康德皇帝身穿军装，看起来有些不自在地站在宝座旁。他想将首都设在沈阳，即满洲帝国的传统所在地，但日本人想要一个由日本建造的首都。他们选择了长春，并将其名字改为新京（“新首都”）。对于谁是满洲国的老板，几乎没有什么伪装。

- 10 -

When Western nations protest the crudity of the
Manchukuoan puppet show they miss the point. The problem
of Japan is not to reconcile outside powers to her seizure
of Manchuria but to rule over a region that is 90 per cent
Chinese. And so the Japanese Army propped up Pu Yi and
his fellow straw men to win over the people of Manchuria
(wherein they have not been entirely unsuccessful) rather
than to delude the rest of the world (wherein they have
utterly failed). To the Japanese the disturbing fact
about Manchuria is that 28,000,000 of its 31,000,000
people are straight Chinese. Most of them emigrated
from North China in the last fifty years. They come
chiefly from the provinces of Hopeh and Shantung, that
dismal region where overpopulation, exhaustion of the
soil by centuries of cultivation, constant floods or
drought caused by reckless deforestation, and bandit
activities combine to produce an almost chronic state of
famine.

To emigrants fleeing from such a country the fertile,
well-watered Manchurian plain seems a land of milk and honey.
Their exodus in recent years is one of the great mass
migrations of history, reaching a peak of about 1,000,000
a year from 1927 to 1930. Hundreds of thousands of these
were migratory coolies who went back to China for the
winter, but most of them settled down for good. Since
the Japanese came in, the flood of migration has been
steadily drying up. Last September 19,000 coolies entered
Manchuria through Dairen and 12,000 left, as against 21,000
arriving and 10,000 leaving in September, 1933. Japan
is neatly impaled on the horns of a dilemma. To develop
Manchuria the Japanese, unable to induce their own people
to leave home, must encourage Chinese immigrants. But
they are aware that China's strength lies not in arms but
in the capacity of her people to settle and breed, and they
are afraid that the sheer pressure of Chinese numbers may
some day force Japan out of Manchuria.

For its purpose, the puppet government works well
enough. The head of each department of the central
government at Hsinking is Chinese, but each has a Japanese
"adviser" to tell him what to do. It would be closer
to the truth to call the Chinese the advisers and the
Japanese the executives. So many Chinese officials left
the country after the downfall of Young Marshal Chang
that it has been hard to find enough able Chinese to go
around even as figureheads. The Minister of Foreign
Affairs, for example, is an amiable, slow-witted Chinaman
named Hsieh-Chieh-shih (see page 87 for his picture), whose
chief qualification for his post seems to be that he
speaks French moderately well. The Vice Minister of
Foreign Affairs is a cocky little rounded-faced Jap named
Ohashi, a self-made man whose career has been made into
a popular novel. Ohashi has a rather nasty sense of
humor. On his desk is a buzzer. When he has drawn up
a document he presses the buzzer and the Minister of
Foreign Affairs hurries in and affixes his signature.

There is an old saying that well expresses the
attitude of the Chinese peasant toward his government:
I dig my well and drink.
I till my land and eat.
I hunt to clothe myself.
Even the power of the Emperor is nothing to me.

当西方国家对满洲国傀儡戏的拙劣提出抗议时，他们并未抓住要点。日本的问题不在于让外部势力接受其对满洲的占领，而在于统治一个百分之九十人口为中国人的地区。因此，日本陆军扶植溥仪及其同伙这些稻草人，是为了赢得满洲民众的支持（在这方面他们并非完全不成功），而不是为了欺骗世界其他地区（在这方面他们彻底失败了）。对日本人来说，满洲令人不安的事实是，在其三千一百万人口中，有两千八百万是纯粹的中国人。其中大多数人是在过去五十年间从中国北方移民而来的。他们主要来自河北和山东两省，那是一个悲惨的地区，人口过剩、数个世纪的耕作导致地力耗尽、因滥伐森林而引发的持续洪涝或干旱，以及匪患活动，共同造成了一种几乎慢性的饥荒状态。

对于逃离这样一个国家的移民来说，肥沃且水源充足的满洲平原似乎是一片流着奶与蜜之地。近年来他们的出走构成了历史上大规模移民潮之一，在1927年至1930年间达到每年约一百万人的峰值。这些移民中有数十万是季节性流动的苦力，他们会在冬季返回中国，但大多数人则永久定居下来。自从日本人进入以来，移民潮一直在稳步消退。去年九月，有一万九千名苦力经大连进入满洲，一万二千人离开；相比之下，1933年九月入境者为两万一千人，出境者为一万人。日本正巧妙地陷入两难境地。为了开发满洲，由于无法诱使本国人民离开家乡，日本人必须鼓励中国移民。但他们意识到，中国的力量不在于武器，而在于其人民定居和繁衍的能力，他们担心纯粹的人口数量压力有朝一日可能会将日本逐出满洲。

就其目的而言，傀儡政府运作得还算良好。位于新京的中央政府各部门首长均为中国人，但每位首长都配有一名日本“顾问”来指示其行事。更贴近事实的说法是，中国人是顾问，而日本人是执行者。在小张少帅垮台后，如此多的中国官员离开了该国，以至于即使只是寻找足够的能人充当门面人物也变得困难。例如，外交总长是一位名叫谢介石的和蔼、迟钝的中国人（见第87页他的照片），他担任此职的主要资格似乎是他法语说得相当不错。外交次长是一个傲慢、圆脸的小个子日本人，名叫大桥（音译），这是一个白手起家的人，其职业生涯已被写成一部流行小说。大桥有一种相当恶劣的幽默感。他的办公桌上有一个蜂鸣器。当他起草好一份文件时，便按下蜂鸣器，外交总长便匆匆进来签署名字。

有一句老话很好地表达了中国农民对其政府的态度：
我掘井而饮。
我耕田而食。
我狩猎以衣身。
即便皇帝之权，于我何干。

- 11 -

The wise man pays such taxes as he must and expects nothing
from the government. To preserve law and order he looks
chiefly to the rule of the family. Byong that, he may
feel a personal loyal to certain leaders, whom he follows
without much regard for the forces behind them. "If the
support of a particular leader can be secured by persuasion
or coercion" comments the Lytton Report, "the support of
his adherents....follows as a matter of course". In setting
up Manchukuo the Japanese followed the lead of the Manchu
Emperors, who filled the high court posts with Manchus but
left local government to the traditional Chinese mandarins.
Puppets the Chinese heads of the state may be, but they are
invaluable to their masters. Sokolsky in the The Tinder Box
of Asia goes so far as to say it is they "who determine the
success of the enterprise. As long as they are willing to
cooperate with Japan, the Japanese will have freedom of
action to carry out their economic and strategic program.
Should they oppose the new state, not even the Japanese Army
can maintain peace there, for an uprising suppressed in one
region would reappear in another."

Two men

CHENG HSIAO-HSU and Jiro Minami are probably
the two most powerful men in Manchukuo today. Tutor and
most trusted adviser of Pu Yi, Cheng is Prime Minister of
the new state. As Commander of the Kwantung Army and
Japanese Ambassador to Pu Yi, Minami controls the army that
keeps the new regime in power and he represents the nation
that pulls the puppet strings.
The conflicting cultures of China and Japan must
be harmonized if the new state is to survive. Neither can
get along without the other. The sharp contrast between
an Oriental China and a Westernized Japan is clearly illumined
by the contrast between the personalities of Cheng and
Minami.

The Prime Minister

CHENG HSIAO-HSU (Su K'an to his friends) is
probably the most intelligent person in Manchukuo. He is
an old man of seventy-five, with a wise, gentle face and the
lips of a poet. Like most Chinese gentlemen of the old
school, he writes poetry and is an expert calligrapher.
The Japanese seem to have a penchant for calligraphers: Yuan
Chin-kai, whom they made Mayor of Mukden, is also known well
for his calligraphy. But Cheng is far from a mere dilettante.
He is one of the greatest living poets of China, and in a
land where calligraphy is a fine art, Cheng is famous for
his skill. Collectors pay well for specimens from his brush,
schoolboys study facsimiles of his writing. As a painter
he is also renowned, especially for his pine trees. But
Cheng is no bewildered dreamer blinking owlishly in the
dazzling light that beats upon a throne. The conduct of
great affairs is nothing new to him. He has fought bandits,
governed provinces, run railways before. He has been a
diplomat, an adviser to Emperors, a major-domo-- always with
honor and credit. Only a very old civilization could
produce so remarkable a synthesis of the poet and the man of
action. As he walks into a room there is an enlightened
dignity about him that suddenly makes the button-headed
Jap officers look brutal, clumsy, somewhat ridiculous. He
is a puppet who dominates his puppeteers. He is the man of
whom Sir Reginald Johnston, tutor to Pu Yi, wrote: "In
twenty-five years of experience in China I had never met a
Chinese for whom I had conceived a greater respect and
admiration."

明智之人缴纳必要的税赋，并对政府不抱任何期望。为了维持法律和秩序，他主要依靠家族统治。除此之外，他可能会对某些领导人产生个人忠诚，追随他们时并不太在意其背后的势力。“如果可以通过劝说或胁迫获得某位领导人的支持，”李顿报告评论道，“那么其追随者的支持____也就随之而来”。在建立满洲国时，日本人效仿了满洲皇帝的做法，即由满人占据朝廷高官职位，而将地方政府留给传统的中国官吏。虽然中国的国家元首是傀儡，但他们对主子来说是无价的。索科尔斯基在《亚洲的火药桶》一书中甚至说，正是他们“决定了这项事业的成功。只要他们愿意与日本合作，日本人在执行其经济和战略计划时就拥有行动自由。如果他们反对这个新国家，即使是日本军队也无法在那里维持和平，因为在一个地区被镇压的起义会在另一个地区重新出现。”

两个人

郑孝胥和南次郎可能是当今满洲国最有权势的两个人。作为溥仪的导师和最信任的顾问，郑孝胥是这个新国家的总理。作为关东军司令官和日本驻溥仪大使，南次郎控制着维持新政权权力的军队，并代表着操纵傀儡线的国家。如果要让这个新国家生存下去，就必须调和中日两种冲突的文化。双方缺一不可。东方化的中国与西化日本之间的鲜明对比，通过郑孝胥和南次郎个性的对比得到了清晰的阐明。

总理

郑孝胥（朋友们称他为苏戡）可能是满洲国最聪明的人。他是一位七十五岁的老人，面容睿智温和，有着诗人般的嘴唇。像大多数旧学派的中国绅士一样，他写诗，并且是书法专家。日本人似乎对书法家情有独钟：袁金凯，他们任命其为奉天市长，也以其书法闻名。但郑孝胥绝不仅仅是一个业余爱好者。他是当今中国最伟大的诗人之一，在这个书法被视为一门精细艺术的土地上，郑孝胥以其技艺闻名。收藏家们重金购买他的墨宝，学童们研习他书法的摹本。作为一名画家，他也享有盛誉，尤其擅长画松树。但郑孝胥并不是一个在王座耀眼的强光下眨巴着眼睛、困惑的梦想家。处理重大事务对他来说并不新鲜。他以前曾剿匪、治理省份、经营铁路。他曾担任外交官、皇帝顾问、大管家——始终享有荣誉和信誉。只有非常古老的文明才能孕育出诗人与实干家如此非凡的结合体。当他走进房间时，身上散发出一种开明的尊严，突然使得那些留着板寸头的日本军官显得残暴、笨拙，甚至有些可笑。他是一个支配着操纵者的傀儡。庄士敦爵士，溥仪的导师，曾这样写道：“在我二十五年的中国经历中，我从未遇到过一位让我产生更大敬意和钦佩的中国人。”

A single theme runs through Cheng's long and
extraordinary career: his loyalty to the Manchu dynasty.
Because of that he retired to private life when the Manchu
Empire fell, because of that he has come back again as Prime
Minister of Manchukuo. Born of a scholarly family in
Suchow in 1859, he was sent to the Hanliyuan Academy at
the Manchu court. By 1881 he was a civil servant and a
poet of distinction. In 1890 he became secretary to the
Chinese Legation in Tokyo, two years later Consul General
for Kobe and Osaka. Recalled by the Sino-Japanese War, he was
Director of the Peiping-Hankow Railway for five years. He
later became military Governor of Kwangsi province, then suffer-
ing from an epidemic of banditry. After annihilating a
large band, he turned to diplomacy. His eloquence was such
that during his three-year term he completely suppressed
banditry without fighting another battle.
Rewarded with the Star of the Double Dragon Treasure,
Cheng retired to Shanghai and built himself a villa,
Haitsanglou or "The Place Hidden By the Sea," where he happily
wrote poetry and painted pine trees. His retirement was
interrupted by service as an adviser on a proposed Manchurian
railway - he advocated the all-Chinese port of Hulutao, an
idea later taken up by Yong Marshal Chang and a term as
Governor of Hunan province, which was cut short by the 1911
revolution. When the Manchus fell he retired again to
Haitsanglou. "From this event will anarchy take its rise",
Cheng predicted, accurately enough, in a poem written that
year. Steadfastly he refused offers of portfolios in several
republican Cabinets. But when Pu Yi, living a virtual prisoner
in Peiping's Forbidden City, summoned him in 1934, he came
at once. As master of the royal household he undertook to
reform the expensive and corrupt court system. He began by
abolishing his own salary. When Feng, the "Christian General",
threatened the Emperor's life, Cheng devised the plan whereby
he escaped to take refuge in the Japanese Legation. For the
next seven years he was tutor, adviser, and almost father to
Young Pu Yi. He and his son were the companions of Pu Yi
when he journeyed to Manchuria in 1931 to take office as chief
executive of the new state.
In a poem addressed to his eldest son, Cheng once
wrote: "Riches and honors are worth no more than a wild swan's
feather." He could have been one of the richest men in
China - at a slight sacrifice of principle - but he preferred
to live simply in his villa by the sea, supporting himself by
selling specimens of his calligraphy. Display is foreign to
his nature. He has always worn the simplest of Chinese
garments except on two occasions: once when he put on a
military uniform to fight bandits, once when he wore Western
clothes on the journey to Manchuria with Pu Yi. His regimen
as Prime Minister is strenuous enough to wear out a much
younger man. He rises at 3.00 a.m., exercises for an hour
or so, writes poetry or practices calligraphy for two hours,
fortified by a fragrant cup of tea. This is the time he
writes in his journal, which he has been keeping for fifty
years. At breakfast, which consists of a bowl of rice gruel,
he cheerfully surveys the day's work. His office day begins
at eight forty-five and ends with his daily conference with
the Emperor at six in the evening. He goes to bed firmly
at nine every night, not scrupling to leave a banquet to do so.
Tall and spare, he keeps himself in excellent condition.

The commander-in-chief

JIRO MINAMI was born into a samurai family in 1874.
At the age of eleven he was formally dedicated to Mars, when
his father put a wooden tag around his neck and sent him off
to a soldier uncle in Tokyo. Uncle Miyazaki, a wealthy
cavalry captain, spared no effort and expense to make a
soldier out of his nephew. He succeeded. In 1895 young
Jiro was graduated from the Tokyo Military Academy, which

郑孝胥漫长而非凡的职业生涯贯穿着一个主题：他对满清王朝的忠诚。正因为如此，当满清帝国覆灭时，他退隐私生活；也正因为如此，他再次出山担任满洲国总理。他于1859年出生于苏州的一个书香门第，被送往满清朝廷的翰林院。到1881年，他已成为一名公务员和杰出的诗人。1890年，他成为驻东京中国公使馆的秘书，两年后任神户和大阪的总领事。因中日战争被召回后，他担任平汉铁路局局长五年。后来他成为广西省的军事总督，当时该省正遭受匪患流行的困扰。在歼灭一大股土匪后，他转向外交。他的口才如此之好，以至于在三年任期内，他没有再打一仗就完全肃清了匪患。

获赐双龙宝星勋章后，郑孝胥退隐上海，为自己建造了一座别墅，名为“海藏楼”或“隐藏在海边之地”，在那里他愉快地写诗和画松树。他的退休生活因担任拟议中的满洲铁路顾问而中断——他主张使用全中资的葫芦岛港，这一想法后来被小张少帅采纳——以及担任湖南省省长一职，但该任期因1911年革命而缩短。当满清覆灭时，他再次退隐至海藏楼。“从此事变起 anarchic（混乱/无政府状态）”，他在那一年写的一首诗中准确地预测道。他坚定地拒绝了几届共和内阁的部长职位邀请。但是，当实际上被囚禁在北京紫禁城的溥仪于1934年召见他时，他立即前往。作为内务府大臣，他着手改革昂贵且腐败的宫廷制度。他从废除自己的薪水开始。当“基督将军”冯玉祥威胁皇帝生命时，郑孝胥 devised（策划）了使其逃往日本公使馆避难的计划。在接下来的七年里，他是年轻的溥仪的导师、顾问，几乎如同父亲一般。1931年，当溥仪前往满洲就任新国家行政首脑时，他和他的儿子是溥仪的旅伴。

在一首写给长子的诗中，郑孝胥曾写道：“富贵轻于野鸿毛。”他本可以成为中国最富有的人之一——只需稍微牺牲原则——但他更喜欢在海边的别墅里过着简朴的生活，靠出售书法作品自给自足。炫耀与他的本性格格不入。除了两次例外，他总是穿着最简单的中式服装：一次是他穿上军装去剿匪，另一次是他与溥仪前往满洲时穿了西式服装。作为总理，他的日常工作强度足以累垮一个年轻得多的人。他凌晨三点起床，锻炼一小时左右，喝着一杯香茶提神，写诗或练习书法两小时。这是他写日记的时间，他已坚持记日记五十年。早餐是一碗米粥，他愉快地审视当天的工作。他的办公日从八点四十五分开始，到晚上六点与皇帝的每日会晤结束。每晚九点他准时上床睡觉，不惜为此离开宴会。他身材高大瘦削，保持着极佳的身体状态。

总司令

南次郎于1874年出生在一个武士家庭。十一岁时，他正式献身于战神，当时他的父亲在他脖子上挂了一个木牌，把他送到东京的一位军人叔叔那里。宫崎叔叔是一位富有的骑兵上尉，不遗余力也不惜费用地将侄子培养成一名军人。他成功了。1895年，年轻的南次郎从东京陆军士官学校毕业，该校

he later headed. In 1903 he was graduated from the Army
Staff College, just in time for the Russo-Japanese War. He
went in a hard-riding, hard-drinking lieutenant, came out the
same sort of captain, A clever tactician, a strict
disciplinarian, long on action and short on words, Captain
Minami steadily climbed the military ladder: colonel, chief
of cavalry, commander in China, director Military Academy,
vice chief general staff, commander in Korea, member supreme
war council, and, finally, Minister of War in the Wakatsuki
Cabinet.
By this time Jiro Minami had become a red-faced, bull-
necked old soldier. Politicians like Wakatsuki and conciliatory
Baron Shidehara, the Foreign Minister, he regarded as obstacles
in the path of Japan's glorious destiny in Asia, and he made
little effort to conceal his contempt for them. Later
developments have justified him: today the war lord rides
high while his two pacifist opponents are in complete political
eclipse, fortunate, indeed, to have escaped assassination.
Minami was one of the first to make the great discovery, since
exploited to the hilt by the Army clique, that no Japanese
politician will stand up to a uniform. When the "Mukden
incident" of September 18, 1931, started the well-oiled
Japanese Army machine on its conquest of Manchuria, Minami
rode roughshod over the alarmed protests of the Wakatsuki
Cabinet. There are many who even suspect it was a secret
order from him that first set in motion the Army machine.
It is pointed out that in August, 1931, he flatly opposed
the plans of the Wakatsuki Cabinet to reduce the Army and
declared that the Manchurian problem would "exist for a
long time". Six weeks later the Japanese Army began to
devour Manchuria.
Some see in Minami's appointment to the command of
the Army in Manchukuo a portent that the meal is not finished.
The man he relieves, General Hishikari ("Happy Sparrow"),
is no milksop. Erect, iron-jawed, with a penetrating,
almost savage wit, Hishikari is fond of fluttering his lady
guests by declaring: "I came from the wild parts of Japan!
I've never been tamed!" But Hishikari's restless panther
eyes are nothing compared to the cold little eye-slits in
Minami's gray-stubbled military mug. If the Army plans to
move into Inner Mongolia, and there are indications that
it does, Minami is the man to pull it off. Poker-faced -
his constant smile reveals nothing - and diplomatic, he has
successfully steered a middle course in the delicate
maneuvering of Japanese intra-army politics between Nobuyuki
Abe's conservatives and the extremists led by his schoolmate
and successor as War Minister, Sadao Araki. A good listener,
he rarely commits himself. No one quite knows what goes
on inside his large, close-cropped bullet head. But he has
a grim sense of humor. "These machine guns", his War
Office once explained to the world, "are being sent to
relieve Japanese troops in Manchuria, who are suffering
from overwork."
Squat, belligerent Jiro Minami has only one thing in
common with angular, pacifistic ex-Premier Wakatsuki: both
are called "Gozen Sama" ("Mister Morning"), a title popularly
confered on those who drink until the small hours. The
Japanese, lightheaded tipplers as a rule, greatly admire
anyone who can hold his liquor. The "Mister Morning" band
is a small and select group. In his early days Minami
drank from breakfast to bed. As a junior officer in Formosa
he searched vainly for a drinking companion who could keep up
with him. Finally he discovered a corporal who, abashed,

他后来担任该职。1903年，他毕业于陆军大学校，恰逢日俄战争爆发。他入伍时是一名骑马冲锋、嗜酒如命的少尉，退役时仍是同样作风的上尉。作为一名精明的战术家、严格的纪律执行者，他行动多于言语，南次郎（Minami）在军界稳步晋升：上校、骑兵总监、驻华司令官、陆军士官学校校长、参谋本部次长、驻朝鲜司令官、最高战争委员会成员，最后出任若槻内阁的陆军大臣。

此时，南次郎已变成一位面色红润、颈项粗壮的老旧军人。他将若槻（Wakatsuki）等政治家以及主张缓和的外相币原喜重郎男爵（Baron Shidehara）视为日本在亚洲辉煌 destiny 道路上的障碍，并毫不掩饰对他们的蔑视。后来的事态发展证明他是正确的：如今这位军阀权势熏天，而他的两位和平主义对手则在政治上彻底失势，能幸免于暗杀已是万幸。南次郎是最早做出这一重大发现的人之一，此后陆军派系对此加以充分利用，即没有任何日本政客敢与身穿军装者对抗。当1931年9月18日的“沈阳事变”启动这台运转良好的日本陆军机器开始征服满洲时，南次郎粗暴地践踏了若槻内阁惊慌失措的抗议。许多人甚至怀疑，正是他的秘密命令首先启动了这台陆军机器。有人指出，1931年8月，他断然反对若槻内阁削减陆军的计划，并宣称满洲问题将“长期存在”。六周后，日本陆军开始吞并满洲。

有些人认为，任命南次郎指挥满洲国军队是一个迹象，表明这顿大餐尚未吃完。被他接替的菱刈隆将军（General Hishikari，“快乐麻雀”）并非软弱之辈。菱刈隆身材挺拔，下巴坚毅，机智敏锐近乎野蛮，他喜欢通过宣称“我来自日本的荒野之地！我从未被驯服！”来吓唬他的女性客人。但是，菱刈隆那双不安的豹眼，比起南次郎那张布满灰白胡茬的军人面孔上冰冷的细眯眼，简直不值一提。如果陆军计划进入内蒙古——且有迹象表明确实如此——南次郎就是能搞定此事的人。他面无表情——他那恒常的微笑不透露任何信息——且善于外交，在日本陆军内部保守派的阿部信行（Nobuyuki Abe）与由其同学及继任陆军大臣的荒木贞夫（Sadao Araki）领导的极端派之间的微妙政治 maneuvering 中，他成功地采取了中间路线。他是一个很好的倾听者，很少表态。没人确切知道在他那颗硕大、剪着平头的子弹形脑袋里在想什么。但他有一种冷酷的幽默感。“这些机枪”，他的陆军省曾向全世界解释说，“是为了缓解在满洲因过度劳累而受苦的日军部队。”

矮壮、好斗的南次郎与棱角分明、主张和平的前首相若槻只有一个共同点：两人都被称为“御前样”（Gozen Sama，“早晨先生”），这是一个通俗地授予那些饮酒至凌晨时分的人的称号。日本人通常是轻浮的酒徒，非常钦佩任何能喝酒的人。“早晨先生”圈子是一个小而精选的群体。在南次郎早年，他从早餐喝到就寝。在台湾担任下级军官时，他徒劳地寻找能跟上他酒量的酒友。最后他发现了一名下士，后者羞怯地表示，

declared he had no suitable civilian clothes. At once Minami
bought him "a fine drinking kimono". Today Minami drinks
moderately, with meticulous precision, downing two bottles
of sake (rice wine) every evening, nine minutes for the first,
twenty-one minutes for the second. Drinking is all very well
but, proud of his samurai lineage, Minami keeps himself in
good fighting trim. At the age of sixty - five years from
retirement - he is still a passable fencer, an expert with
broadsword and singlestick, a good horseman, and a devoted
archer. When he is in Japan he lives in Kamakura, which
is to Tokyo as Long Island is to New York. Every morning
he walks down to the beach wearing a heavy wooden sword five
feet long. After a strenuous bout of shadow-fencing, he
pounds the nape of his neck with the sword in the firm belief
that he thereby reduces the swelling caused by drinking and
so prolongs his life. He then strolls along the beach for
a half hour or so, lustily trolling out the "Jorkri" songs
of his native province.
The Puppet state of Manchukuo is thirty-four months
old. Supposing that Cheng and Minami were to sit down and
write an interim report, what would they itemize as their
greatest achievements, their sorest failures?

Boom

The first thing travelers in Manchukuo notice is the
boom atmosphere that pervades the South Manchuria Railway
zone. Hsinking, the new capital, is being built up at a
feverish rate; millions of yen have been spent on public
buildings and houses for the Chinese officials and their Jap
"advisers". If one ventures outside the S.M.R. zone, however,
all traces of the boom have vanished - except for the rail-
roads and highways being built under heavy guards of Jap
infantry. The villages are more poverty-stricken, their
inhabitants more tattered than ever. All of which is summed
up in the balance of trade. The 1933 balance was unfavourable
for the first time in fourteen years, and 1934 is going to
be even worse. Low soybean prices have hit exports ($145,000,
000 in 1933 against $211,000,000 in 1932) and imports have
shot upward ($176,000,000 in 1933 against $103,000,000 in 1932).
Imports have been boosted by the big quantities of building
materials brought in by the Japs. During the first seven
months of 1934 iron and steel imports were more than double
the same period in 1933, machinery and tools were up three
times, vehicles one and a half times, cement double. Last
July, for the first time in history, Dairen's trade topped
Shanghai's.
The Chinese peasants who settled Manchukuo, however,
aren't interested in the building boom at Hsinking or Dairen's
rank as a seaport. They have suffered much in the last few
years, partly from the economic dislocation that inevitably
attended cutting Manchuria off from China - loss in trade,
withdrawal of Chinese investments, etc. - and partly from
the price of soybeans already mentioned. Eighty-five per cent
of the people of Manchukuo are farmers; the miserable income
of the average Manchukuoan peasant - family income is estimated
at about one yen (twenty-nine cents) per person per month -
has been seriously reduced. And so one finds that imports of
commodities consumed by the masses have been falling off
as imports of building materials have been increasing. Cotton
piece goods were off a third in the first seven months of 1934,
wheat flour a half, and so on. Bean prices rose last summer,
however, and this year's crop is expected to be smaller than
usual, to the relief of the Japanese authorities.

自己没有合适的便服。南次郎立刻为他买了一件“精美的饮酒和服”。如今南次郎饮酒适度，且讲究精确，每晚喝两瓶清酒（米酒），第一瓶用时九分钟，第二瓶用时二十一分钟。饮酒虽好，但南次郎以武士血统为荣，保持着良好的战斗状态。在六十五岁——距离退休还有五年——的年纪，他仍是一名过得去的剑客，精通大刀和单棍，骑术精良，且热衷于射箭。他在日本时住在镰仓，镰仓之于东京犹如长岛之于纽约。每天早晨，他佩戴一把五英尺长的重型木剑走到海滩。经过一番激烈的空击练习后，他用剑敲击自己的后颈，坚信这样可以减轻因饮酒引起的肿胀，从而延长寿命。随后，他在海滩漫步约半小时，高声吟唱家乡省份的“Jorkri”歌曲。

傀儡国家满洲国已成立三十四个月。假设郑孝胥（Cheng）和南次郎坐下来撰写一份中期报告，他们会将哪些列为最大的成就，哪些列为最痛苦的失败？

繁荣

前往满洲国的旅行者注意到的第一件事，是弥漫在南满铁路（South Manchuria Railway）区域的繁荣气氛。新首都新京（Hsinking）正以狂热的速度建设；数百万日元已花费在公共建筑以及为中国官员及其日本“顾问”建造的房屋上。然而，如果人们冒险走出南满铁路区域，所有繁荣的痕迹都消失了——除了在日本步兵严密守卫下修建的铁路和公路。村庄更加贫困，居民比以往更加衣衫褴褛。这一切都总结在贸易平衡表中。1933年的贸易逆差是十四年来首次出现，而1934年的情况将更加糟糕。大豆价格低迷打击了出口（1933年为1.45亿美元，而1932年为2.11亿美元），进口则急剧上升（1933年为1.76亿美元，而1932年为1.03亿美元）。日本人带入的大量建筑材料推高了进口。1934年前七个月，钢铁进口量是1933年同期的两倍多，机械和工具增加了三倍，车辆增加了一点五倍，水泥增加了一倍。去年七月，大连的贸易额历史上首次超过上海。

然而，定居满洲国的中国农民对新京的建筑热潮或大连作为海港的地位并不感兴趣。他们在过去几年中遭受了许多苦难，部分原因是将满洲从中国割裂开来不可避免地导致的经济混乱——贸易损失、中国投资撤出等——部分原因则是前述的大豆价格问题。满洲国85%的人口是农民；普通满洲国农民的悲惨收入——估计家庭人均月收入约为1日元（29美分）——已严重减少。因此，人们发现，随着建筑材料进口的增加，大众消费品的进口却在下降。1934年前七个月，棉布进口减少了三分之一，小麦面粉减少了一半，等等。然而，去年夏天豆类价格上涨，且预计今年的收成将少于往常，这让日本当局松了一口气。

Bank notes

The pretty poster on page 86 stands for the greatest
achievement of Manchukuo so far: the stabilization of the
currency. Under the Changs the people of Manchuria lived in
a fantastic world of fluctuating and conflicting currencies.
Everyone printed money, from the provincial banks down to
the kaoliang distillers, and it rarely occurred to anyone to
redeem his paper. Most of these currencies had an extremely
local popularity and a hectic history. All sorts of foreign
money was also floating around - Chinese silver dollars,
popular then as now because hard money has long been a rarity
in Manchuria, Japanese yen in the S.M.R. zone, Russian rubles
up north around Harbin. Confusion was worse confounded by
the war lords, who printed emergency money and sometimes
executed bankers tactless enough to trade in it at market
rather than face value.
One of the first things the Japanese Army did was to
seize the Chinese banks of issue, as a measure of "self-defense".
Private deposits were generally recognized, but the chief
assets, large sums put in by officials of the Chang regime,
were confiscated. The three provincial banks and Young
Chang's Frontier Bank were merged into the Central Bank of
Manchu, which announced an ambitious program of stabilization.
The Manchukuoan yuan was established, a managed currency
that is artificially kept at an exchange parity with the
Chinese silver dollar. Although it is probably not backed
up by "at least 50 per cent gold and silver" as is officially
claimed, the yuan is vastly preferable to previous currencies.
It is strong enough to sell at a premium over the Japanese
Yen. The Central Bank announced that after July 1, 1934,
the former currencies would become legally worthless. It
would continue to redeem most of them at fixed rates, however,
up to July 1, 1935. By last July, according to the bank's
figures, 93.1 per cent of the old money had been exchanged
for new. Even allowing for propagandist exaggeration,
this part of the program would seem to be a success.

Budget

The new currency is one boast of the Japanese. The
other is that Manchukuo's budget has been in balance for the
three fiscal years of the new state's existence. The 1934-
25 budget adds up to $64,500,000 and, except for a small
highway loan, is perfectly balanced. A further point of
pride is the budget's composition. Salt taxes and levies
on the peasants, direct and indirect, used to supply the
bulk of Young Marshal Chang's revenue; the Japanese have
reduced salt taxes, making up for them by raising customs
duties. The Changs spent 80 per cent of their state
revenues on military purposes; the Japanese have reduced
this item to 30 per cent. In Jehol province the opium poppy
was cultivated on a big scale and revenues from opium made
General Tang Yu-lin, Governor of the province under the
Changs, a very wealthy man; the Japanese claim to have
brought opium growing under strict control and to derive no
revenue therefrom.
All these protestations are in part true, but each
needs a skeptical footnote. The budget is balanced, but
(1) no one knows how accurate the given figures are, (2) no
one knows whether Japan or the S.M.R. has been making secret
loans to Manchukuo. Military expenditures have been reduced
to 30 per cent, but this is merely because the burden of
maintaining the new regime has been shifted to the Japanese
Army, which is paid for out of Japan's pocket. In the fiscal

纸币

第86页那张精美的海报代表了满洲国迄今为止最大的成就：货币稳定。在张氏家族统治下，满洲人民生活在一个汇率波动且货币冲突的奇幻世界中。从省级银行到高粱酿酒厂，每个人都在印钞，而且几乎没人想到要兑现他们的纸币。大多数这些货币仅在极局部地区流行，且历史动荡不安。各种外币也在流通——中国银元，因其硬通货在满洲长期稀缺而像现在一样受欢迎；南满铁路区域的日元；哈尔滨北部地区的卢布。军阀们使混乱雪上加霜，他们印发紧急货币，有时甚至处决那些不够圆滑、按市场汇率而非面值交易这些货币的银行家。

日本陆军采取的最初措施之一，就是以“自卫”为名接管中国的发钞银行。私人存款通常得到承认，但主要资产，即张氏政权官员存入的大笔资金，被没收。三家省级银行和张学良的边业银行合并为满洲中央银行，该行宣布了一项雄心勃勃的稳定计划。满洲国元得以确立，这是一种管理货币，人为地保持与中国银元的汇率平价。虽然它可能不像官方声称的那样有“至少50%的金银”作为支撑，但满洲国元远优于之前的货币。其强度足以以高于日元的溢价出售。中央银行宣布，1934年7月1日后，旧货币将在法律上失效。然而，该行将继续以固定比率兑换大部分旧货币，直至1935年7月1日。根据该行的数据，截至去年七月，93.1%的旧货币已兑换为新货币。即使考虑到宣传性的夸大，该计划的这一部分似乎也是成功的。

预算

新货币是日本人的吹嘘之一。另一项吹嘘是，在新国家存在的三个财政年度中，满洲国的预算一直保持平衡。1934-25年度的预算总额为6,450万美元，除了一笔小额公路贷款外，完全平衡。另一个值得骄傲之处是预算的构成。盐税和对农民的直接及间接征税曾是张小帅（Young Marshal Chang）收入的主要来源；日本人降低了盐税，并通过提高关税来弥补。张氏家族将其国家收入的80%用于军事目的；日本人已将此项降至30%。在热河省，鸦片罂粟曾大规模种植，鸦片收入使张氏统治下的该省省长汤玉麟将军成为非常富有的人；日本人声称已将鸦片种植置于严格控制之下，并从中不获取任何收入。

所有这些声明部分属实，但每一项都需要加上一个怀疑的注脚。预算是平衡的，但（1）没人知道所给数据的准确性如何，（2）没人知道日本或南满铁路公司是否一直在向满洲国提供秘密贷款。军事支出已降至30%，但这仅仅是因为维持新政权的负担已转移给日本陆军，其费用由日本国库支付。在财政

year of 1933 Japan spent $41,600,000 on its Manchurian forces,
which is considerably more than the Changs ever spent in a
year. Japan's claims about opium are discounted especially
heavily by observers. The government Opium Monopoly Bureau
has set strict quotas for poppy growing, but these don't
seem to mean much. Even the Japanese blushed slightly when
the official Kirin Province Government Gazette on January
29, 1934, published on the same page the 1934 quota of the
Opium Monopoly as 10,400,000 liangs and the estimated yield
for 1934 as 19,400,000 liangs. Such control as there is
seems chiefly designed to produce revenue. Despite a lot
of high-powered propaganda about "rationing" every opium
smoker in Manchukuo, travelers find the sale of opium wide
open from Dairen, where Japanese peddlers made a fat living,
to Harbin, where numerous little shops sell heroin, morphine,
and opium to Russian school children for twenty cents a shot.
This last has been explained as a pleasant little devise of
the Japanese to undermine the Russians, whom they don't
much like.

Bandits

MANCHURIA is the traditional hom of banditry.
The country folk call them "hung-hutze" or "Red Beards",
according to some authorities because the bands were originally
made up of Russian fugitives from Siberia, according to
others because Manchurian bandits used to tie on huge red
beards to scare people. Summer and fall are the bandit
seasons, for the eight-foot stalks of mature kaoliang then
give excellent shelter to lurking bandits. One rule is
observed by all bandit bands: never kidnap a woman. Bitter
experience has convinced them that (1) she invariably causes
dissension in their band and (2) most Chinamen figure it is
cheaper and more fun to buy a new wife than to ransom the
old one.
The Japanese claim they have reduced the bandits
of Manchukuo from 200,000 to a mere 40,000. Their efforts
have been heroic, but impartial observers think there is at
least as much banditry in Manchukuo today as there was under
Young Marshal Chang. In 1932 Manchukuo spent $15,700,000,
42 per cent of its total budget, for bandit suppression.
This doesn't include the cost of maintaining 80,000 Japanese
soldiers in Manchukuo who spend a large part of their time
chasing bandits. The real point is that no one agrees on
just what is and what isn't a bandit. The Japanese apply
the term to all hostile forces, much as all opposing Nicaraguans
were bandits to the U.S. Marines. Actually Manchurian
bandits today may be (1) real, professional Redbeards carrying
on a traditional calling, (2) remnants of the 200,000 soldiers
Young Marshal Chang left behind him when he skipped over the
Great Wall, (3) patriotic Chinese youths carrying on the
same sort of guerrilla warfare that Francis Marion waged
against the British redcoats in the Carolina swampland, or
(4) farmers ruined by floods and low soybean prices.
To protest against society a French-man riots,
a Russian sabotages, an Englishman writes to the Times, a
Yankee votes the Democratic ticket, and a Manchukuonan turns
to banditry. Its prevalence is a social barometer. The
glass is falling rapidly just at present. According to
Ben Dorfman's recent Foreign Policy Association report on
Two Years of the Manchukuo Regime, the Japs made some progress
in restoring peace and order in 1933 but have lost ground
again of recent months. Last October, for instance, the
Redbeards performed such versatile feats as raiding a primary
school and carrying off three teachers and a hundred pupils,
ambushing fifty Manchu cavalrymen and killing forty-six of
them, derailing a train loaded with Japanese soldiers, derailing
and looting a freight train, attacking a road-construction
camp and killing two Japanese, and kidnapping a provincial

1933年，日本在其满洲军队上花费了41,600,000美元，这比张氏家族在任何一年的花费都要多得多。观察家们尤其不看好日本关于鸦片的说法。政府鸦片专卖局虽然为罂粟种植设定了严格的配额，但这些似乎并无多大意义。甚至当1934年1月29日的官方《吉林省政府公报》在同一页上刊登鸦片专卖局1934年的配额为10,400,000两，而1934年的预计产量为19,400,000两时，连日本人都有些脸红。现有的管制似乎主要是为了创收。尽管有关在满洲国对每位鸦片吸烟者实行“配给制”的高调宣传甚嚣尘上，但旅行者发现，从日本小贩借此大发横财的大连，到众多小店以每针20美分的价格向俄国学童出售海洛因、吗啡和鸦片的哈尔滨，鸦片销售都是完全公开的。最后这一点被解释为日本人削弱他们不太喜欢的俄国人的一种令人愉快的小计谋。

匪患

满洲是匪患的传统发源地。乡下人称之为“红胡子”（hung-hutze），据一些权威人士称，这是因为匪帮最初由来自西伯利亚的俄国逃犯组成；另一些人则称，这是因为满洲土匪过去常系上巨大的红胡子来吓唬人。夏季和秋季是匪患季节，因为那时成熟的高粱杆高达八英尺，为潜伏的土匪提供了极佳的掩护。所有匪帮都遵守一条规则：绝不绑架妇女。痛苦的经验使他们确信：(1) 女人 invariably（总是）会在他们的帮派中引起纷争；(2) 大多数中国人认为，买个新老婆比赎回旧老婆更便宜也更有趣。

日本人声称他们已将满洲国的土匪从20万人减少到区区4万人。他们的努力可谓英勇，但公正的观察家认为，如今满洲国的匪患至少与少帅张治下时期一样严重。1932年，满洲国花费了15,700,000美元用于剿匪，占其总预算的42%。这还不包括维持在满洲国的80,000名日本士兵的费用，这些士兵大部分时间都在追捕土匪。真正的问题在于，没有人就究竟什么是土匪、什么不是土匪达成一致。日本人将所有敌对势力都称为土匪，就像所有反对美国海军陆战队的尼加拉瓜人都被美军视为土匪一样。实际上，如今的满洲土匪可能是：(1) 从事传统行当的真正职业“红胡子”；(2) 少帅张跳过长城时留下的20万士兵的残余；(3) 进行着与弗朗西斯·马里恩（Francis Marion）在卡罗来纳沼泽地对英国红衫军进行的游击战类似行动的爱国中国青年；或 (4) 因洪水和低大豆价格而破产的农民。

为了抗议社会，法国人举行暴动，俄国人进行破坏，英国人给《泰晤士报》写信，美国佬投票支持民主党，而满洲国人则投身匪患。其普遍程度是社会气压计。目前，这根指针正在迅速下降。根据本·多夫曼（Ben Dorfman）最近关于《满洲国政权两年》的外交政策协会报告，日本人在1933年在恢复和平与秩序方面取得了一些进展，但在最近几个月又失去了阵地。例如，去年十月，“红胡子”上演了各种多才多艺的壮举：袭击一所小学，带走三名教师和一百名学生；伏击五十名满洲骑兵并杀死其中四十六人；使一列载有日本士兵的火车脱轨；使一列货运列车脱轨并抢劫；袭击一个筑路营地并杀死两名日本人；以及绑架了一位省**〔此处转录不清〕**

"Bandits are like flies," says sardonic General
Hishikari, ex-commander in Manchukuo, who should know.
"Slap at them, they disappear. But they come back some-
where else." The Japanese have done a lot of slapping.
The South Manchuria Railway allows no stalk of bandit-shleting
kaoliang to grow within several hundred yards of its roadbed.
It also makes great efforts to win the favor of villages
along its tracks and gets them to report bandits. Propaganda
units follow in the wake of the Army's punitive expeditions,
hoping to convert such bandits as survive. The offer of
a job building railroads or even hunting other bandits is
the best argument. Sometimes the process is achieved with
magical quickness. To a traveler who asked to see a real
Manchurian bandit a local police official explained, "It
is impossible. You see, we industrialize them immediately".
But the industrialization has still a long way to go and even
now one is safe from bandits only inside the heavily guarded
S.M.R. zone. Such peaceful activities as playing golf and
mending roads are carried on under the protecting rifles
of Japanese soldiers. Banditry is the most pressing problem
of the new state now and in the immediate future.

Bang goes the open door!

If the powers regard Manchukuo as part of China,
let them deal with China," suggested the Japanese Foreign
Office playfully. "Yes, they can appeal to China." And
that was all the satisfaction the powers got out of Japan.
Their grievance was a real one. The oil business is the
biggest non-Japanese business in Manchukuo and it was
threatened with extinction. Apparently it was to be
delivered into the hands of the Manchuria Oil Co., whose
stock was 80 per cent Japanese, 20 per cent Manchukuoan
controlled. Wherefore Socony-Vacuum, which has 300 agencies
in Manchukuo and sells, or did sell, half the gasoline
consumed there, and Royal Dutch Shell and Texas Oil Co. were
much disturbed. And with them their respective governments
There were front-page headlines for a while and the State
Department wrote some sharp notes, but when the uproar
subsided the Manchuria Oil Co. was still in possession of its
monopoly on oil sales. The open door, which the powers,
including Japan, had years ago solemnly pledged themselves
to maintain in China, had obviously been closed. The ingenuity
of the Japanese Foreign Office in explaining it away was
dazzling: the open door hadn't discriminate against any
nation; it had been closed perhaps maybe but Manchukuo isn't
part of China and hence the open door doesn't apply to her;
Japan "merely declared publicly" she would respect the open
door, is "not committed" to do so; and finally, Manchukuo
is independent and what business is it of Japan's anyway?
The connection between the open door and the
recognition of Manchukuo is a matter of debate. So far only
Japan and El Salvador have recognized the new state.
Salvador's Consul General in Tokyo frankly declared it was
"Purely a matter of business, the outgrowth of El Salvador's
acute need of new markets for her coffee." Last summer
Emperor Kang Teh bestowed a princely tip on Salvador, a
10,000-yen check for the relief of hurricane victims. Even
unofficial gestures such as the recent goodwill trip through
the country of the British Industries Mission are much
appreciated: the Britishers went home with orders in their
pockets for $40,000,000 (reported) worth of railway supplies

“土匪就像苍蝇，”曾任满洲国司令官的菱刈（Hishikari）将军讽刺地说道，他应该对此有所了解。“你拍打它们，它们就消失了。但它们又会出现在其他地方。”日本人已经进行了大量的拍打。南满铁路公司不允许在其路基几百码范围内生长任何一株可供土匪藏身的高粱。它还大力争取沿线村庄的好感，让它们报告土匪。宣传部门跟随在军队的惩罚性远征队之后，希望能转化那些幸存的土匪。提供一份修建铁路甚至追捕其他土匪的工作是最好的论据。有时，这一过程以神奇的速度完成。当一名旅客要求看一名真正的满洲土匪时，当地警察官员解释说：“这不可能。你看，我们立即将他们工业化了。”但这种工业化还有很长的路要走，即使在现在，人们只有在戒备森严的南满铁路（S.M.R.）区域内才能免受土匪之害。打高尔夫球和修路等和平活动都是在日本士兵的保护性步枪下进行的。匪患是这个新国家当前及近期最紧迫的问题。

“门户开放”砰然关闭！

“如果列强将满洲国视为中国的一部分，那就让他们去与中国打交道吧，”日本外务省戏谑地建议道。“是的，他们可以向中国申诉。”这就是列强从日本那里得到的全部满足。他们的不满是真实的。石油业务是满洲国最大的非日资业务，它面临着灭绝的威胁。显然，它将被移交给满洲石油公司（Manchuria Oil Co.）手中，该公司的股份80%由日本人控制，20%由满洲国人控制。因此，拥有300家代理机构并在满洲国销售（或曾经销售）了一半汽油的美孚真空油公司（Socony-Vacuum），以及皇家荷兰壳牌公司和德克萨斯石油公司都深感不安。它们的各自政府也是如此。头版头条轰动了一阵子，国务院也写了一些措辞严厉的信函，但当喧嚣平息后，满洲石油公司仍然垄断着石油销售。列强（包括日本）多年前曾庄严承诺在中国维持的“门户开放”，显然已经关闭。日本外务省在解释此事时的巧思令人眼花缭乱：门户开放并没有歧视任何国家；它也许可能已经关闭，但满洲国不是中国的一部分，因此门户开放不适用于她；日本只是“公开声明”她将尊重门户开放，并不“承诺”这样做；最后，满洲国是独立的，这关日本什么事呢？

门户开放与承认满洲国之间的联系是一个有争议的问题。到目前为止，只有日本和萨尔瓦多承认了这个新国家。萨尔瓦多驻东京总领事坦率地宣称，这“纯粹是商业问题，源于萨尔瓦多为其咖啡寻找新市场的迫切需求。”去年夏天，康德皇帝慷慨地赏赐了萨尔瓦多一笔王子般的 tip（小费/赏金），一张用于救济飓风受害者的10,000日元支票。即使是像最近英国工业代表团在该国进行的善意访问这样的非官方姿态，也受到高度赞赏：英国人回家时口袋里装着价值40,000,000美元（据报道）的铁路用品

and steel. A French group is preparing to follow them.
"America is idealistic", the Honorable Hiroshi Saito, Japanese
Ambassador to the U.S., recently observed. "And idealism
in international affairs is a luxury".
In Korea today there is not a single foreign bank
and very few foreign firms of any kind. Observers expect
Manchukuo to repeat the pattern. Certainly the Japanese
Empire supplied 44 per cent of Manchuria's imports in
1929 and supplies over 66 per cent today. The lucrative
trade of foreign machinery and armament firms with the
Changs' great arsenal at Mukden is now entirely in Japanese
hands. No foreign investments of any consequence have
been made since 1931 and the foreign colony in Manchukuo
has been reduced from 143,000 in 1938 to less than 75,000
today. Automobiles are believed to be the next subject
for a state monopoly. The Chrysler Corp. got its fingers
burned last fall when the Kwantung Government, obviously
acting for the Army, revoked its license to build an assembly
plant in Dairen.
The closing of the open door would be more serious
were it not for the microscopic size of non-Japanese foreign
investments in Manchukuo anyway. The Japanese in 1930
had 70 per cent of all foreign investments, Soviet Russia
26 per cent, England 2 per cent, the U.S. and France 1 per
cent apiece. The English have a small interest in the
profitable Peiping-Mukden Railway, and the British-American
Tobacco Co. dominates the tobacco trade - though there is
now talk of a tobacco monopoly. The total U.S. investment
is only $4,500,000. The Russian investment is mostly
in the famed Chinese Eastern Railway, which the Czar built,
the French paid for, and the Soviet owns. Manchukuo has
offered some $50,000,000 for the Russian half interest in
the road, and negotiations have been dragging on for months.
When and if the deal goes through, practically all the
foreign investments in Manchukuo will be Japanese.

The future: Army vs. Chinese

There is every reason to expect that the Japanese
will give Manchukuo a more honest, efficient, and benevolent
government than ever was its lot under the Changs. For one
thing, they have a motive: it would be almost impossible to
use Manchukuo as a strategic base in the next war if its
people were hostile. Also, Japs have the technical ability
to govern well. Their own form of government, after which
the new state is roughly patterned, it notable efficient.
Like all war lords, the Changs were in Manchuria only for
what they and their henchmen could get out of it. Nor did
they have any notion of good government. Their administration
was wasteful, corrupt, and inefficient. No one worried
very much about the appalling leakage in taxes: 90 per cent
of all taxes collected never reached the central government
at all. They spent 80 per cent of such revenues as they
got for military purposes - on an army of 250,000 men and
on the famous $100,000,000 arsenal at Mukden. The Lytton
Commission, while not approving Japanese rule for Manchuria,
definitely opposed return to the Chang regime.
But the Japanese will find that it is not enough
to rule well. They must also rule wisely. Westernized as
they try to be, they regard efficiency as the summum bonum
of government. Not so the old-style Chinese, who look on
bungling and graft with all the indulgence of a Tammany
ward heeler. "He who is not in office," admonished
Confucius, "has no concern with the administration of its
duties". If the Japanese are not careful, they will alienate
their Chinese partners in Manchukuo by giving them too good
a government. Korea is a case in point. Since Japan took
it over in 1910 she has administered that dismal, poverty-
pinched land efficiently enough. But the Japanese, like the
