和钢铁订单。一个法国团体正准备效仿他们。“美国人是理想主义的，”日本驻美国大使斋藤博（Hiroshi Saito）阁下最近观察到。“而在国际事务中，理想主义是一种奢侈品”。

如今的朝鲜没有一家外国银行，也几乎没有外国公司。观察家预计满洲国将重演这一模式。毫无疑问，1929年日本帝国供应了满洲44%的进口商品，而如今这一比例超过66%。外国机械和军火公司与张氏在沈阳的大型兵工厂之间的有利可图的贸易现在完全掌握在日本人手中。自1931年以来，没有任何具有重大意义的外国投资，满洲国的外国侨民人数已从1938年的143,000人减少到如今的不足75,000人。汽车被认为是下一个国家垄断的目标。克莱斯勒公司（Chrysler Corp.）去年秋天吃了亏，当时关东政府显然代表陆军行事，撤销了在大连建立组装厂的许可证。

如果不是因为在满洲国的非日资外国投资规模微乎其微，“门户开放”的关闭将会更加严重。1930年，日本人占据了所有外国投资的70%，苏俄占26%，英国占2%，美国和法国各占1%。英国人在利润丰厚的北宁铁路（Peiping-Mukden Railway，即京奉铁路）中拥有少量权益，而英美烟草公司主导着烟草贸易——尽管现在有关于烟草垄断的传闻。美国总投资额仅为4,500,000美元。俄国的投资主要在于著名的中东铁路，这条铁路由沙皇建造，法国人出资，苏联拥有。满洲国已出价约50,000,000美元购买俄国在该铁路的一半权益，谈判已拖延数月。当且如果这笔交易达成，满洲国的几乎所有外国投资都将属于日本。

未来：军队 vs 中国人

我们有充分理由期待，日本人将给予满洲国一个比张氏统治时期更加诚实、高效和仁慈的政府。首先，他们有一个动机：如果其人民怀有敌意，几乎不可能在下一场战争中利用满洲国作为战略基地。此外，日本人具备良好治理的技术能力。新国家大致模仿的日本政府形式以其高效著称。像所有军阀一样，张氏在满洲只是为了他们及其亲信能从中捞取利益。他们对良政也没有任何概念。他们的行政机构浪费、腐败且低效。没人太担心税收惊人的流失：征收的所有税款中有90%根本没有到达中央政府。他们将所得收入的80%用于军事目的——供养一支25万人的军队和维护沈阳那座著名的价值100,000,000美元的兵工厂。李顿调查团虽然不赞成日本对满洲的统治，但明确反对回归张氏政权。

但是，日本人会发现，仅仅治理得好是不够的。他们还必须治理得明智。尽管他们试图西化，但他们将效率视为政府的最高善（summum bonum）。老派中国人并非如此，他们以坦慕尼协会（Tammany）街区小政客般的宽容看待笨拙和贪污。“不在其位，不谋其政，”孔子告诫道。如果日本人不小心，他们会通过给他们的中国伙伴提供过于良好的政府而疏远他们。朝鲜就是一个例证。自从日本在1910年接管以来，她对那片凄凉、贫困的土地进行了足够有效的管理。但是，日本人，就像

Germans, are too unimaginative and inflexible, too arrogantly nationalistic to be good colonists. Their rule, beneficent in material ways perhaps, is tactless, overbearing, heedless of native psychology. It is resented by the Koreans with an ever increasing bitterness. Observers trace a damning parallel between Japanese methods in Manchukuo today and in Korea thirty years ago. The expressions of loyalty to the new regime from chambers of commerce and other native bodies mean nothing. The archives at Seoul, capital of Korea, one apprehensively notes, contain bushels of the same sort of thing.
Whether the Army mind will ever grasp the subtleties of Chinese psychology seems doubtful. Recently the traditional provinces of Manchuria were split into smaller districts. The purpose of the move was reasonable enough: to reduce the power of the provincial governors and make it easier to extend the central authority over them. But many cool heads on civilian shoulders doubt whether the country is yet ripe of so drastic an upsetting of tradition. Nor is the direct-action policy of the Army calculated to win popular sympathy. The police chief at Mukden put it bluntly: "The Manchurian population does not enjoy the military administration. The Army has fired all the villages along a road stretching twenty miles between Shanchengchen and Tunghua, alleging that they were harbouring bandits. We question whether that is the way to enhance the Manchurian people's friendship." Because Mongolia is the possible theatre of the next Russo-Japanese war (see map on page 82) and the probable next addition to Manchukuo, the Army has made a special effort to be nice to the 2,000,000 Mongols of Manchuria. It has set aside the huge province of Hsingan (not included in the recent split-up) as a special Mongol preserve. Hsingan has more autonomy than the other districts of Manchukuo, and the Japs have forbidden Chinese settlers to invade it. Considering all this, the recent news of a mutiny among Mongol troops in the Manchukuoan Army is discouraging.
No amount of tact can do away with a certain amount of ill will caused by the very efficiency of the new government. Taxes are lighter and more impartially collected than in the days of the Changs and justice is dispensed more equally. The result is that many persons "privileged" for one reason or another have lost their special standing. By the same token, officials who once luxuriated in "squeeze" and bribe money now must get along on a comparatively unexciting salary. Stabilized currency is fine, but it means ruin to thousands of money-changers and speculators. New roads and railroads open up the land but they also deprive large numbers of farmers of their only paying winter job, carting produce over the frozen rivers to distant railroads.

The futures: Army vs. civil service

The real threat to Manchukuoan stability, however, comes not from the Chinese but from the Japanese themselves. The Army conquered Manchuria, the Army set up the Pu Yi regime, and now the Army wants to run the country. It would like to take over the whole structure of Japanese interests built up in Manchuria during the past thirty years. There is, not unnaturally, opposition.
The lesser but currently more threatening conflict is between the Army and the civilian officials in the Kwantung Leased Territory. Soon after the Army began its Manchurian operations, it also began a steady encroachment on the sphere of the Kwantung Civil Government. The civil officials and the police, threatened with loss of "face",

德国人缺乏想象力和灵活性，民族主义傲慢自大，难以成为优秀的殖民者。他们的统治在物质方面或许有益，但处事笨拙、专横跋扈，无视当地人的心理。朝鲜人对此的怨恨与日俱增。观察家们指出，日本目前在满洲国的手段与三十年前在朝鲜的手段之间存在着令人谴责的相似之处。商会及其他本地团体对新政权的效忠表态毫无意义。人们不安地注意到，朝鲜首都首尔的档案中充斥着大量此类文件。

军方思维能否领会中国心理的微妙之处，似乎值得怀疑。最近，传统的东北各省被划分为较小的行政区。这一举措的目的尚属合理：削弱省督的权力，使中央当局更容易对其实施控制。但许多冷静的文职人员怀疑，国家是否已成熟到足以承受如此剧烈的传统颠覆。此外，军方的直接行动政策也无助于赢得民众的同情。沈阳警察局长直言不讳地说：“满洲民众并不喜欢军事管制。军队以窝藏匪徒为由，烧毁了山城镇与通化之间长达二十英里道路沿线的所有村庄。我们怀疑这是否是增进满洲人民友谊的方式。”由于蒙古可能是下一次日俄战争的潜在战场（见第82页地图），并可能成为满洲国的下一个扩张目标，军队特别努力对满洲的200万蒙古人示好。它划出了巨大的兴安省（未包含在最近的行政区划调整中）作为专门的蒙古人保留地。兴安省比满洲国其他地区拥有更多的自治权，且日本人禁止中国移民侵入该地。鉴于此，近期关于满洲国军队中蒙古部队发生兵变的消息令人沮丧。

无论多么圆滑的手腕，都无法消除因新政府的高效率而引发的某种程度的敌意。税收比张氏军阀时期更轻，征收也更公正，司法分配更为平等。结果是，许多因各种原因享有“特权”的人失去了其特殊地位。同样，那些曾经沉迷于“敲竹杠”和贿赂收入的官员，现在必须依靠相对平淡的薪水度日。货币稳定固然好，但这意味着成千上万的钱庄老板和投机者面临破产。新公路和铁路的开发开辟了土地，但也剥夺了大量农民唯一的有偿冬季工作——通过冰封的河流将农产品运往远处的铁路线。

未来展望：军队 vs. 文官系统

然而，对满洲国稳定的真正威胁并非来自中国人，而是来自日本人自己。军队征服了满洲，建立了溥仪政权，现在军队想要统治这个国家。它希望接管过去三十年在满洲建立起来的整个日本利益结构。这种 opposition（反对）是自然而然的。

目前较小但更具威胁性的冲突发生在军队与关东租借区的文职官员之间。军队开始其在满洲的行动后不久，便开始稳步侵蚀关东民政当局的势力范围。文职官员和警察面临“丢面子”的威胁，

vigorously resisted. The tension increased until this fall came the "reform plan" that put the Army in charge of the Kwantung police. The 15,000 officials of the Kwantung Government threatened to resign in a body. The police talked of open revolt. Even the hardboiled General Hishikari, then Commander of the Kwantung Army and Governor of the Kwan-tung Territory, was impressed. When his efforts at conciliation failed, he wired Tokyo advising the plan be dropped. The Army's reply was to replace Hishikari with Minami, about two minutes harder boiled. The reform plan is going right ahead. Any opposition is to be dealt with in the only way the Army knows - by force. Martial law is already in the air.

The future: Army vs.capitalists

A certain Japanese industrialist, discreetly anonymous, recently summed it up: "Our people do not seem to realize that the political right and left do not move away from each other in a straight line. They travel in a circle and the extreme right and the extreme left are exactly the same. Thus, while our government spends its time and its money to run down Communists, it spends even more time and even more money to attain the Communist objective from another direction. Manchukuo, despite the fact that it is controlled by adherents of the extreme right, seems to be growing up into a fine example of a socialist state." For chapter and verse of his accusation the anonymous industrialist could have turned to a document entitled The True Meaning of National Defense, which was broadcast last spring to the tune of 160,000 copies by the military authorities. Its phraseology was such as one finds in the Daily Worker - "uneven distribution of wealth," "poverty of the masses," "ineffectual State control". It suggested a thoroughgoing reformation of the economic structure, advocated greater state control over private interest so as "to advance the happiness of the nation as a whole."
The Army wants to set up state socialism in Manchukuo. The capitalists want freedom to exploit the country. The outcome of this conflict, part of a broader

进行了 vigorous（激烈）抵抗。紧张局势不断升级，直到今年秋天出台了将关东警察置于军队控制之下的“改革计划”。关东政府的15,000名官员威胁集体辞职。警察扬言公开叛乱。即使是当时担任关东军司令兼关东州长官的铁腕人物菱刈隆将军也深受震动。当他的调解努力失败后，他致电东京建议放弃该计划。军方的回应是用南次郎取代菱刈隆，后者比前者还要强硬几分。改革计划正在顺利推进。任何反对意见都将以军队唯一知晓的方式——武力——来处理。戒严令已隐约可见。

未来展望：军队 vs. 资本家

一位谨慎匿名的日本实业家最近总结道：“我国人民似乎没有意识到，政治上的左派和右派并不是沿直线相互远离的。它们在一个圆圈中运行极右派和极左派完全相同。因此，虽然我们的政府花费时间和金钱打击共产党人，但它却花费更多的时间和金钱从另一个方向实现共产主义的目标。尽管满洲国由极右派支持者控制，但它似乎正成长为一个社会主义国家的典范。”这位匿名实业家的指控有据可查，他可以引用去年春天由军事当局散发16万份的一份题为《国防真义》的文件。其措辞如同《每日工人报》中的用语——“财富分配不均”、“大众贫困”、“国家控制不力”。它建议对经济结构进行彻底改革，主张加强对私人利益的国家控制，以便“促进整个国家的幸福”。

军队希望在满洲国建立国家社会主义。资本家希望拥有剥削该国的自由。这场冲突的结果，作为更广泛

of the Kwantung Army is "adviser" to the Department of
Industry. "Military men complain that private capital is
not rushing to invest its money in Manchuria," comments one
Japanese newspaper. "Why should it? The government is
running or plans to run everything... No industry of any
importance is left to the private industrialist". The Army
is developing Manchuria's resources primarily for military
reasons, and it wants no interference from capitalists.

The future: Army vs. S.M.R.

The last great champion of capitalism in Manchukuo is
the South Manchuria Railway (see Fortune, February, 1932, for
a detailed account). Of the $500,000,000 invested up to
1931 by Japan in Manchuria, $300,000,000 went into the S.M.R.
and its subsidiaries. The Japanese Government owns 51 per
cent of S.M.R. stock, which it paid for by turning over to
the railroad a hundred-foot strip of territory along its
roadbed that bulges out here and there to include choice
sections of various cities, the Fushun coal mines, the Anshan
iron deposits, and so on. The other 49 per cent is held
by Mitsui, Mitsubishi, and other Japanese banks and investors.
From 1905, when Japan took over the railroad from Russia
after the Russo-Japanese War, up to 1931, Japan's interests
in Manchuria crystallized around the S.M.R. It was, and is,
a great deal more than 691 miles of excellent roadbed, some
500 powerful modern locomotives, some 8,000 freight cars, and
some 550 sleek, luxurious passenger cars. It has only some
$78,000,000 invested in railroading. The rest is made up
of such items as coal mines ($34,000,000) and municipal under-
takings ($42,000,000). The S.M.R. made Dairen second only
to Shanghai among Chinese ports and perhaps the most modern
port on the mainland of Asia. It has played a big part in
developing Manchuria's huge soybean crop, and its agricultural
experts instruct Manchurian farmers in the mysteries of
tractors and crop diversification. It has its own schools
and its public-health service fights bubonic plague throughout
South Manchuria. It is impossible to imagine Manchuria
without the S.M.R.
The Army well knows that so long as the S.M.R. remains
the colossus of Manchukuo the power of the military will be
